example.goal: Explain what the function `rekey_all` in `ai/services/credential_rekey.py` does and when it is called. Answer only; do not plan or change anything.
example.answer:
rekey_all(old_secret=None, apply=False) in ai/services/credential_rekey.py re-encrypts every stored credential value that begins with the 'enc:' prefix (ENC_PREFIX) from the OLD encryption key to the CURRENT key. It computes old_key (the Fernet key derived from old_secret, or the SECRET_KEY-derived fallback when old_secret is None) and new_key (get_fernet_key()), and returns early with same_key=True if they're identical. It then scans all rows with value__startswith=ENC_PREFIX across AISetting plus any extra models listed in settings.AI_EXTRA_CREDENTIAL_MODELS. For each row: if it already decrypts with the new key it's counted as already_current and left alone; otherwise it tries the old key — if that fails the row is added to the 'unreadable' list and never touched; if it succeeds and apply=True the value is re-encrypted with the new key and saved (update_fields=['value']), counted in 'rewritten'. With apply=False it's a dry run that only reports. It returns a dict: {rewritten, already_current, unreadable, same_key, applied}.

When it's called: by the Django management command `manage.py rekey_ai_keys` (ai/management/commands/rekey_ai_keys.py), which invokes rekey_all(old_secret=options['old_key'], apply=options['apply']) — typically after setting a private WEALTHFLOW_AI_ENCRYPTION_KEY, to migrate existing encrypted AI provider keys / Paymob secrets / per-user keys to the new key. It's also exercised directly in ai/tests/test_credential_rekey.py. I did not run any tests or commands; this is a read-only explanation.

## Skill: django-architecture
# Django architecture (WealthFlow)
- Stack: Django 6 backend, vanilla-JS single-page app (no framework), SQLite in the repo (`db.sqlite3` tracked on purpose, never edit it).
- Layers: `core/models/` (one file or folder per area) -> `core/services/<area>/` (business rules) -> `core/views/` (thin JSON views) -> `core/urls/*_urls.py` (all routes `api/...`).
- Views are class-based `View`s returning `JsonResponse`. Start each handler with `_api_auth_required(request)` (from `core.validators`); body via `parse_json_body(request)`.
- Business logic belongs in a service class, never in a view. Reuse the existing service the screen already uses (e.g. `ExpenseService`) instead of writing to models directly.
- Plan gating: wrap routes with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (`core/services/billing`). Sysadmin-only views use `SysadminRequiredMixin`.
- App settings live in `AppSettings` (`AppSettings.get(key, default, user=...)`); `user=None` = global. The AI app's own `ai_*`/`speech_*`/`image_gen_*` settings live in `ai.models.AISetting` (same get/set API). Prefer a UI setting over `.env`.
- `ai/` must not import `core`: WealthFlow-specific AI code lives in `core/ai_pack` and plugs in through `settings.AI_PACKS`; host answers (admin check, audit, currency) are `AI_*` hooks in `wealthflow/settings.py` (`ai/host.py`).
- Every code file must stay <= 200 lines: split into a package folder with an `__init__.py` that re-exports.
- Shared central services are additive-only: `CurrencyConversionService`, `base_currency.py`, `ExchangeRateHistoryService`, `market_profile.py`, settings access. List every caller before touching one.


## Skill: testing
# Testing
- Django tests: `core/tests/<area>/test_*.py`; run `python manage.py test core.tests.<area>` (targeted first, then the full suite). One known sandbox-only failure: the Playwright single-page-failure-isolation test; known on main: `test_speech_api` Arabic Piper test.
- Users in tests get currencies/categories automatically: use `get_or_create`, not `create`.
- Static checks: `python -m pyflakes core tests scripts wealthflow doc_engine manage.py`, `npm run validate`, `python manage.py check`, `makemigrations --check`.
- Browser E2E: `scripts/run_full_e2e.py --headless` on the owner's PC only. Every change adds a module under `tests/modules/<name>.py`, wired in `scripts/e2e_module_dispatch.py`, `scripts/test_ui_human_full_e2e.py` and `tests/core/reporter.py` (page denominators).
- Never claim a test passed unless its command finished successfully; say plainly what was NOT run.
- Automated gate: `python scripts/agent_verify.py` (checks, targeted tests, pyflakes, migrations, i18n, line limits).


## Skill: migrations
# Migrations
- Numbered files in `core/migrations/` (`00NN_name.py`). Create with `python manage.py makemigrations core -n <name>`; check with `python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run` (must report no changes).

- A new model must also be added to the backup order in `core/services/backup_serializer/export_order.py` or `core/tests/system/test_backup_coverage.py` fails.
- Data migrations must be reversible or say plainly why not. Never touch `db.sqlite3` by hand.
- After a model change, check `ai/knowledge/` (`python manage.py generate_ai_knowledge`) and revert incidental `ai/knowledge/` and `db.sqlite3` diffs before delivery.


## Skill: deployment
# Deployment
- Local: Windows + PowerShell, `python manage.py runserver 8000`, Ollama for the AI (`setup-ollama.bat`, guide: `WealthFlow Deployment & Ollama Setup Guide.txt`).
- Production target: PythonAnywhere (env-driven hardening in `wealthflow/settings.py`; DEBUG and tracked `.env`/`db.sqlite3` are accepted only until selling).
- Scheduled work runs through `python manage.py run_automation` (purge of deleted accounts, rates, recurring transactions): it must be scheduled in the host's Tasks.
- Payments: Paymob (test mode + regional accounts); webhook is the only CSRF-exempt endpoint.
- Never push or commit from the agent. Deliver files + `COMMIT_MESSAGE.txt` + `IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.txt`.

- Model: `core/models/expenses.py` (`Expense`, `ExpenseCategory`, `ExpenseSubcategory`). `Expense` has owner, date, year, month, category, amount, `amount_base`, `exchange_rate`, currency, bank, payment_method (Cash / Card / Bank Transfer / Other).

## Skill: django-architecture
# Django architecture (WealthFlow)
- Stack: Django 6 backend, vanilla-JS single-page app (no framework), SQLite in the repo (`db.sqlite3` tracked on purpose, never edit it).
- Layers: `core/models/` (one file or folder per area) -> `core/services/<area>/` (business rules) -> `core/views/` (thin JSON views) -> `core/urls/*_urls.py` (all routes `api/...`).
- Views are class-based `View`s returning `JsonResponse`. Start each handler with `_api_auth_required(request)` (from `core.validators`); body via `parse_json_body(request)`.
- Business logic belongs in a service class, never in a view. Reuse the existing service the screen already uses (e.g. `ExpenseService`) instead of writing to models directly.
- Plan gating: wrap routes with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (`core/services/billing`). Sysadmin-only views use `SysadminRequiredMixin`.
- App settings live in `AppSettings` (`AppSettings.get(key, default, user=...)`); `user=None` = global. The AI app's own `ai_*`/`speech_*`/`image_gen_*` settings live in `ai.models.AISetting` (same get/set API). Prefer a UI setting over `.env`.
- `ai/` must not import `core`: WealthFlow-specific AI code lives in `core/ai_pack` and plugs in through `settings.AI_PACKS`; host answers (admin check, audit, currency) are `AI_*` hooks in `wealthflow/settings.py` (`ai/host.py`).
- Every code file must stay <= 200 lines: split into a package folder with an `__init__.py` that re-exports.
- Shared central services are additive-only: `CurrencyConversionService`, `base_currency.py`, `ExchangeRateHistoryService`, `market_profile.py`, settings access. List every caller before touching one.

# Testing
- Django tests: `core/tests/<area>/test_*.py`; run `python manage.py test core.tests.<area>` (targeted first, then the full suite). One known sandbox-only failure: the Playwright single-page-failure-isolation test; known on main: `test_speech_api` Arabic Piper test.

example.answer:
Two places import/call `build_data_slice` from `core/ai_pack/knowledge/data_slice.py`:

1. `core/ai_pack/pack.py` (lines 33–35): the `_data_slice` wrapper imports it and is registered as the `data_slice` extension hook (`reg.add_extension("data_slice", _data_slice)`, line 65). It needs it to provide the host-pack implementation of the data-slice hook that the `ai/` layer calls generically.

2. The indirect caller is `ai/views/ai_chat/chat_pipeline/workflow.py` (line 54), which calls `ak.build_data_slice(user)` — that name comes from `ai/services/app_knowledge/__init__.py` (line 24), whose `build_data_slice` does NOT import the core function itself; it dispatches through the `ext("data_slice")` hook registered by the pack. It needs the slice as a short, owner-scoped description of the user's own setup (base currency, owned asset types, bank count, expense categories) to include as optional context in workflow how/where/should chat answers.

So the real consumer is the AI chat workflow pipeline; `core/ai_pack/pack.py` is the only direct importer, acting as the WealthFlow host adapter.

## Skill: django-architecture
# Django architecture (WealthFlow)
- Stack: Django 6 backend, vanilla-JS single-page app (no framework), SQLite in the repo (`db.sqlite3` tracked on purpose, never edit it).
- Layers: `core/models/` (one file or folder per area) -> `core/services/<area>/` (business rules) -> `core/views/` (thin JSON views) -> `core/urls/*_urls.py` (all routes `api/...`).
- Views are class-based `View`s returning `JsonResponse`. Start each handler with `_api_auth_required(request)` (from `core.validators`); body via `parse_json_body(request)`.
- Business logic belongs in a service class, never in a view. Reuse the existing service the screen already uses (e.g. `ExpenseService`) instead of writing to models directly.
- Plan gating: wrap routes with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (`core/services/billing`). Sysadmin-only views use `SysadminRequiredMixin`.
- App settings live in `AppSettings` (`AppSettings.get(key, default, user=...)`); `user=None` = global. The AI app's own `ai_*`/`speech_*`/`image_gen_*` settings live in `ai.models.AISetting` (same get/set API). Prefer a UI setting over `.env`.
- `ai/` must not import `core`: WealthFlow-specific AI code lives in `core/ai_pack` and plugs in through `settings.AI_PACKS`; host answers (admin check, audit, currency) are `AI_*` hooks in `wealthflow/settings.py` (`ai/host.py`).
- Every code file must stay <= 200 lines: split into a package folder with an `__init__.py` that re-exports.
- Shared central services are additive-only: `CurrencyConversionService`, `base_currency.py`, `ExchangeRateHistoryService`, `market_profile.py`, settings access. List every caller before touching one.


## Skill: security-and-tenancy
# Security and multi-tenancy
- Every user-owned row has an `owner` FK. Query with `Model.objects.filter(owner=request.user)` or the helpers in `core/validators/ownership.py` (`_owned_queryset`, `_owned_object_or_404`, `_child_owned_*`). No staff or superuser bypass.
- Child rows inherit ownership through their parent (e.g. salary entries via `company__owner`).
- Start every API view with `_api_auth_required(request)`. CSRF is on everywhere except the Paymob webhook. Login attempts use django-axes.
- Settings and secrets: AI provider keys are encrypted (`credential_encryption.py`); never log or return them. `.env` and `db.sqlite3` are never edited.
- Non-admins only get a whitelist from `/api/settings/`. Source-code tools of the AI are sysadmin-only.
- Every security-relevant change needs a test proving user A cannot read or change user B's data (pattern in the tests of `ai/tests/test_ai_chat_manage.py`).

- Numbered files in `core/migrations/` (`00NN_name.py`). Create with `python manage.py makemigrations core -n <name>`; check with `python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run` (must report no changes).

example.goal: Explain what the function `rekey_all` in `ai/services/credential_rekey.py` does and when it is called. Answer only; do not plan or change anything.
example.answer:
`rekey_all` (ai/services/credential_rekey.py:25) migrates stored encrypted credentials to the current encryption key. It works as follows:

1. Determines the old Fernet key — the one derived from the given `old_secret`, or the default SECRET_KEY-derived fallback when `old_secret` is None — and the new key from `get_fernet_key()` (the private WEALTHFLOW_AI_ENCRYPTION_KEY). If both keys are identical it returns immediately with `same_key: True`.
2. Scans every row whose `value` starts with the `enc:` prefix across the credential stores: the `AISetting` model plus any models listed in `settings.AI_EXTRA_CREDENTIAL_MODELS` (e.g. `core.AppSettings`, which holds Paymob secrets).
3. For each row: if it already decrypts with the new key it is counted as `already_current` and left alone; otherwise it tries the old key — if that fails the row is listed in `unreadable` and never touched; if the old key reads it, the row is re-encrypted with the new key and saved (only when `apply=True`) and counted in `rewritten`.
4. Returns a dict with `rewritten`, `already_current`, `unreadable`, `same_key`, and `applied`.

When it is called: it is invoked by the management command `ai/management/commands/rekey_ai_keys.py` (`manage.py rekey_ai_keys`, with `--apply` to actually write changes; without it the command is a dry run). This is the operator step after setting a private `WEALTHFLOW_AI_ENCRYPTION_KEY` on a server whose stored keys were still encrypted with the default server key — the UI also surfaces this instruction via the `ai_default_key_warning` setting notice. It is not called at runtime by any view or service, only by that management command (and by the tests in `ai/tests/test_credential_rekey.py`).

## Skill: django-architecture
# Django architecture (WealthFlow)
- Stack: Django 6 backend, vanilla-JS single-page app (no framework), SQLite in the repo (`db.sqlite3` tracked on purpose, never edit it).
- Layers: `core/models/` (one file or folder per area) -> `core/services/<area>/` (business rules) -> `core/views/` (thin JSON views) -> `core/urls/*_urls.py` (all routes `api/...`).
- Views are class-based `View`s returning `JsonResponse`. Start each handler with `_api_auth_required(request)` (from `core.validators`); body via `parse_json_body(request)`.
- Business logic belongs in a service class, never in a view. Reuse the existing service the screen already uses (e.g. `ExpenseService`) instead of writing to models directly.
- Plan gating: wrap routes with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (`core/services/billing`). Sysadmin-only views use `SysadminRequiredMixin`.
- App settings live in `AppSettings` (`AppSettings.get(key, default, user=...)`); `user=None` = global. The AI app's own `ai_*`/`speech_*`/`image_gen_*` settings live in `ai.models.AISetting` (same get/set API). Prefer a UI setting over `.env`.
- `ai/` must not import `core`: WealthFlow-specific AI code lives in `core/ai_pack` and plugs in through `settings.AI_PACKS`; host answers (admin check, audit, currency) are `AI_*` hooks in `wealthflow/settings.py` (`ai/host.py`).
- Every code file must stay <= 200 lines: split into a package folder with an `__init__.py` that re-exports.
- Shared central services are additive-only: `CurrencyConversionService`, `base_currency.py`, `ExchangeRateHistoryService`, `market_profile.py`, settings access. List every caller before touching one.


## Skill: testing
# Testing
- Django tests: `core/tests/<area>/test_*.py`; run `python manage.py test core.tests.<area>` (targeted first, then the full suite). One known sandbox-only failure: the Playwright single-page-failure-isolation test; known on main: `test_speech_api` Arabic Piper test.
- Users in tests get currencies/categories automatically: use `get_or_create`, not `create`.
- Static checks: `python -m pyflakes core tests scripts wealthflow doc_engine manage.py`, `npm run validate`, `python manage.py check`, `makemigrations --check`.
- Browser E2E: `scripts/run_full_e2e.py --headless` on the owner's PC only. Every change adds a module under `tests/modules/<name>.py`, wired in `scripts/e2e_module_dispatch.py`, `scripts/test_ui_human_full_e2e.py` and `tests/core/reporter.py` (page denominators).
- Never claim a test passed unless its command finished successfully; say plainly what was NOT run.
- Automated gate: `python scripts/agent_verify.py` (checks, targeted tests, pyflakes, migrations, i18n, line limits).


## Skill: balances-and-net-worth
# Balances and net worth
- `BalanceEntry` (`core/models/balance/balance_entry.py`): owner, title, `balance_type` (cash / bank / gold / certificate), bank, currency, amount (Decimal 18,2).
- Money moves through `core/services/expenses/expense_balance_helpers.py` (`_apply_expense_balance_delta`) and the balance services in `core/services/balance/`. Never change a balance with a raw `.update()` outside these helpers.
- Net worth: `core/services/balance/net_worth_calculations.py` and `net_worth_service/`. These are financial calculations: do not change without approval.
- Cash expenses and bank expenses both reduce a matching `BalanceEntry`; a missing matching entry raises `matching_balance_entry_not_found`, too little money raises `insufficient_balance`.
- Always use `Decimal`, never `float`, for stored money. Amounts are kept in their own currency plus `amount_base` in the user's base currency (`get_user_base_code(owner)`).
- Latest exchange rates: `core/services/shared/latest_rates.latest_exchange_rates()`; never `order_by("-fetched_at").first()` inline.
- Tests: `core/tests/balance/`.


## Skill: expenses
# Expenses
- Model: `core/models/expenses.py` (`Expense`, `ExpenseCategory`, `ExpenseSubcategory`). `Expense` has owner, date, year, month, category, amount, `amount_base`, `exchange_rate`, currency, bank, payment_method (Cash / Card / Bank Transfer / Other).
- Write ONLY through `ExpenseService.create_expense / update_expense / delete_expense(…, owner)` in `core/services/expenses/expense_service.py`: they check ownership, convert currency (`CurrencyConversionService.strict_rate`) and adjust the balance in one transaction.
- Errors are `ValueError` codes: `bank_account_required`, `category_not_found`, `matching_balance_entry_not_found`, `insufficient_balance`, `readonly_mirrored_expense`, `exchange_rate_missing`.
- Rows with `source_type` set are read-only mirrors of fixed-asset records: they cannot be edited or deleted directly.
- Views: `core/views/expense_views.py`, `expense_category_views.py`, `expense_summary_views.py`. Frontend: `static/js/expenses/`.
- Tests: `core/tests/expenses/`; E2E: `tests/modules/expenses/`.


## Skill: migrations
# Migrations
- Numbered files in `core/migrations/` (`00NN_name.py`). Create with `python manage.py makemigrations core -n <name>`; check with `python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run` (must report no changes).

- Child rows inherit ownership through their parent (e.g. salary entries via `company__owner`).

example.answer: build_monthly_summary(by_month, format_currency) in core/ai_pack/providers/expenses_provider/aggregation.py takes two inputs: by_month — a dict mapping (year, month) tuples to dicts that each contain a 'total' (number) and a 'count' — and format_currency — a callable used to format amounts. It returns a list of dicts, one per (year, month) key, sorted in reverse chronological order (newest month first). example.goal: Where is `feature_required` (defined in `ai/host.py`) used in this project? List the files and say what each one does with it. Answer only; do not plan or change anything.
example.answer:
`feature_required` is defined in `ai/host.py` (line 53) as a view-decorator hook: it delegates to the `AI_FEATURE_GATE` hook (set by the host), defaulting to open. It is used in three files:

1. **`ai/urls_chat.py`** — imports it (line 5) and wraps every AI chat/speech route with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")`: speech capabilities/transcribe/synthesize, AI chat, voice chat + sentence poll, conversation list/detail/search, attachment upload/detail, block confirm/cancel, message rewind/export/feedback, progress, chat mode, memory list/detail, and AI stop views.

2. **`ai/urls_platform.py`** — imports it (line 4) and stores it in a module-level alias `_ai = feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (line 6) to apply the same plan gate to the platform AI routes defined there.

3. **`core/ai_pack/urls.py`** — imports it (line 4) and wraps the `api/financial-advisor/ai/insights/` route (`AIInsightsView`) with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (line 8).

Note: there is a separate, same-named `feature_required` in `core/services/billing/decorators.py` (re-exported from `core/services/billing/__init__.py`) — that is the billing plan/feature decorator, distinct from the `ai/host.py` hook version; `core/ai_pack/host.py` bridges it by importing the billing one and returning `feature_required(flag)` as the gate.

## Skill: django-architecture
# Django architecture (WealthFlow)
- Stack: Django 6 backend, vanilla-JS single-page app (no framework), SQLite in the repo (`db.sqlite3` tracked on purpose, never edit it).
- Layers: `core/models/` (one file or folder per area) -> `core/services/<area>/` (business rules) -> `core/views/` (thin JSON views) -> `core/urls/*_urls.py` (all routes `api/...`).
- Views are class-based `View`s returning `JsonResponse`. Start each handler with `_api_auth_required(request)` (from `core.validators`); body via `parse_json_body(request)`.
- Business logic belongs in a service class, never in a view. Reuse the existing service the screen already uses (e.g. `ExpenseService`) instead of writing to models directly.
- Plan gating: wrap routes with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (`core/services/billing`). Sysadmin-only views use `SysadminRequiredMixin`.
- App settings live in `AppSettings` (`AppSettings.get(key, default, user=...)`); `user=None` = global. The AI app's own `ai_*`/`speech_*`/`image_gen_*` settings live in `ai.models.AISetting` (same get/set API). Prefer a UI setting over `.env`.
- `ai/` must not import `core`: WealthFlow-specific AI code lives in `core/ai_pack` and plugs in through `settings.AI_PACKS`; host answers (admin check, audit, currency) are `AI_*` hooks in `wealthflow/settings.py` (`ai/host.py`).
- Every code file must stay <= 200 lines: split into a package folder with an `__init__.py` that re-exports.
- Shared central services are additive-only: `CurrencyConversionService`, `base_currency.py`, `ExchangeRateHistoryService`, `market_profile.py`, settings access. List every caller before touching one.


## Skill: testing
# Testing
- Django tests: `core/tests/<area>/test_*.py`; run `python manage.py test core.tests.<area>` (targeted first, then the full suite). One known sandbox-only failure: the Playwright single-page-failure-isolation test; known on main: `test_speech_api` Arabic Piper test.
- Users in tests get currencies/categories automatically: use `get_or_create`, not `create`.
- Static checks: `python -m pyflakes core tests scripts wealthflow doc_engine manage.py`, `npm run validate`, `python manage.py check`, `makemigrations --check`.
- Browser E2E: `scripts/run_full_e2e.py --headless` on the owner's PC only. Every change adds a module under `tests/modules/<name>.py`, wired in `scripts/e2e_module_dispatch.py`, `scripts/test_ui_human_full_e2e.py` and `tests/core/reporter.py` (page denominators).
- Never claim a test passed unless its command finished successfully; say plainly what was NOT run.
- Automated gate: `python scripts/agent_verify.py` (checks, targeted tests, pyflakes, migrations, i18n, line limits).


## Skill: migrations
# Migrations
- Numbered files in `core/migrations/` (`00NN_name.py`). Create with `python manage.py makemigrations core -n <name>`; check with `python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run` (must report no changes).
- Never edit or delete a migration that is already in the repo's history; add a new one. Protected by `coding_agent/config.json`.
- A new model must also be added to the backup order in `core/services/backup_serializer/export_order.py` or `core/tests/system/test_backup_coverage.py` fails.
- Data migrations must be reversible or say plainly why not. Never touch `db.sqlite3` by hand.
- After a model change, check `ai/knowledge/` (`python manage.py generate_ai_knowledge`) and revert incidental `ai/knowledge/` and `db.sqlite3` diffs before delivery.


## Skill: deployment
# Deployment
- Local: Windows + PowerShell, `python manage.py runserver 8000`, Ollama for the AI (`setup-ollama.bat`, guide: `WealthFlow Deployment & Ollama Setup Guide.txt`).
- Production target: PythonAnywhere (env-driven hardening in `wealthflow/settings.py`; DEBUG and tracked `.env`/`db.sqlite3` are accepted only until selling).
- Scheduled work runs through `python manage.py run_automation` (purge of deleted accounts, rates, recurring transactions): it must be scheduled in the host's Tasks.
- Payments: Paymob (test mode + regional accounts); webhook is the only CSRF-exempt endpoint.
- Never push or commit from the agent. Deliver files + `COMMIT_MESSAGE.txt` + `IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.txt`.


## Skill: expenses
# Expenses
- Model: `core/models/expenses.py` (`Expense`, `ExpenseCategory`, `ExpenseSubcategory`). `Expense` has owner, date, year, month, category, amount, `amount_base`, `exchange_rate`, currency, bank, payment_method (Cash / Card / Bank Transfer / Other).
- Write ONLY through `ExpenseService.create_expense / update_expense / delete_expense(…, owner)` in `core/services/expenses/expense_service.py`: they check ownership, convert currency (`CurrencyConversionService.strict_rate`) and adjust the balance in one transaction.
- Errors are `ValueError` codes: `bank_account_required`, `category_not_found`, `matching_balance_entry_not_found`, `insufficient_balance`, `readonly_mirrored_expense`, `exchange_rate_missing`.

# Expenses
- Model: `core/models/expenses.py` (`Expense`, `ExpenseCategory`, `ExpenseSubcategory`). `Expense` has owner, date, year, month, category, amount, `amount_base`, `exchange_rate`, currency, bank, payment_method (Cash / Card / Bank Transfer / Other).

- Errors are `ValueError` codes: `bank_account_required`, `category_not_found`, `matching_balance_entry_not_found`, `insufficient_balance`, `readonly_mirrored_expense`, `exchange_rate_missing`.
- Rows with `source_type` set are read-only mirrors of fixed-asset records: they cannot be edited or deleted directly.

## Skill: testing
# Testing
- Django tests: `core/tests/<area>/test_*.py`; run `python manage.py test core.tests.<area>` (targeted first, then the full suite). One known sandbox-only failure: the Playwright single-page-failure-isolation test; known on main: `test_speech_api` Arabic Piper test.

## Skill: django-architecture
# Django architecture (WealthFlow)
- Stack: Django 6 backend, vanilla-JS single-page app (no framework), SQLite in the repo (`db.sqlite3` tracked on purpose, never edit it).
- Layers: `core/models/` (one file or folder per area) -> `core/services/<area>/` (business rules) -> `core/views/` (thin JSON views) -> `core/urls/*_urls.py` (all routes `api/...`).
- Views are class-based `View`s returning `JsonResponse`. Start each handler with `_api_auth_required(request)` (from `core.validators`); body via `parse_json_body(request)`.
- Business logic belongs in a service class, never in a view. Reuse the existing service the screen already uses (e.g. `ExpenseService`) instead of writing to models directly.
- Plan gating: wrap routes with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (`core/services/billing`). Sysadmin-only views use `SysadminRequiredMixin`.
- App settings live in `AppSettings` (`AppSettings.get(key, default, user=...)`); `user=None` = global. The AI app's own `ai_*`/`speech_*`/`image_gen_*` settings live in `ai.models.AISetting` (same get/set API). Prefer a UI setting over `.env`.

- Every code file must stay <= 200 lines: split into a package folder with an `__init__.py` that re-exports.

- Vanilla JS, one file per concern under `static/js/<area>/`, <= 200 lines each. No bundler: scripts are loaded in order from `templates/partials/scripts/0N_*.html` (AI workspace = `04_ai.html`). Line order is load order.

- Plan gating: wrap routes with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (`core/services/billing`). Sysadmin-only views use `SysadminRequiredMixin`.
- App settings live in `AppSettings` (`AppSettings.get(key, default, user=...)`); `user=None` = global. The AI app's own `ai_*`/`speech_*`/`image_gen_*` settings live in `ai.models.AISetting` (same get/set API). Prefer a UI setting over `.env`.

example.goal: Explain what the function `all_refusals` in `ai/services/scope_text.py` does and when it is called. Answer only; do not plan or change anything.
example.answer:
`all_refusals()` in `ai/services/scope_text.py` (line 55) builds and returns the set of every possible refusal wording the AI can produce: the generic no-information text (`ai_scope_no_info`) plus the domain-specific variants (`ai_scope_refused_business`, `ai_scope_refused_app`, `ai_scope_refused_locked`) with their `current`/`other` domain-name placeholders filled in — all of them in each of the four UI languages (en, ar, fr, de). In other words it enumerates the exact strings that `refusal()` (line 43) can generate.

It is called from exactly one place: `is_no_info(content)` in `ai/services/domain_scope.py` (line 40-41), which does `str(content).strip() in scope_text.all_refusals()` to recognize a saved refusal reply. `is_no_info` is then used in two chat-pipeline spots: `response_finalizer.py`'s `is_non_answer()` (line 34) so that no file/download offer is ever attached to a refusal answer, and `chat_pipeline/investigate.py` (line 117) to treat the reply as a no-information case. Tests in `core/tests/ai_pack/test_chat_domains.py` and `core/tests/ai_pack/from_ai/test_guide_files_and_refusals.py` also exercise it indirectly. In short: it is the reference set used at reply-finalization time to detect "this saved answer is a refusal" so the UI never offers it as an exportable file.

## Skill: django-architecture
# Django architecture (WealthFlow)
- Stack: Django 6 backend, vanilla-JS single-page app (no framework), SQLite in the repo (`db.sqlite3` tracked on purpose, never edit it).
- Layers: `core/models/` (one file or folder per area) -> `core/services/<area>/` (business rules) -> `core/views/` (thin JSON views) -> `core/urls/*_urls.py` (all routes `api/...`).
- Views are class-based `View`s returning `JsonResponse`. Start each handler with `_api_auth_required(request)` (from `core.validators`); body via `parse_json_body(request)`.
- Business logic belongs in a service class, never in a view. Reuse the existing service the screen already uses (e.g. `ExpenseService`) instead of writing to models directly.
- Plan gating: wrap routes with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (`core/services/billing`). Sysadmin-only views use `SysadminRequiredMixin`.
- App settings live in `AppSettings` (`AppSettings.get(key, default, user=...)`); `user=None` = global. The AI app's own `ai_*`/`speech_*`/`image_gen_*` settings live in `ai.models.AISetting` (same get/set API). Prefer a UI setting over `.env`.
- `ai/` must not import `core`: WealthFlow-specific AI code lives in `core/ai_pack` and plugs in through `settings.AI_PACKS`; host answers (admin check, audit, currency) are `AI_*` hooks in `wealthflow/settings.py` (`ai/host.py`).
- Every code file must stay <= 200 lines: split into a package folder with an `__init__.py` that re-exports.
- Shared central services are additive-only: `CurrencyConversionService`, `base_currency.py`, `ExchangeRateHistoryService`, `market_profile.py`, settings access. List every caller before touching one.


## Skill: testing
# Testing
- Django tests: `core/tests/<area>/test_*.py`; run `python manage.py test core.tests.<area>` (targeted first, then the full suite). One known sandbox-only failure: the Playwright single-page-failure-isolation test; known on main: `test_speech_api` Arabic Piper test.
- Users in tests get currencies/categories automatically: use `get_or_create`, not `create`.
- Static checks: `python -m pyflakes core tests scripts wealthflow doc_engine manage.py`, `npm run validate`, `python manage.py check`, `makemigrations --check`.
- Browser E2E: `scripts/run_full_e2e.py --headless` on the owner's PC only. Every change adds a module under `tests/modules/<name>.py`, wired in `scripts/e2e_module_dispatch.py`, `scripts/test_ui_human_full_e2e.py` and `tests/core/reporter.py` (page denominators).
- Never claim a test passed unless its command finished successfully; say plainly what was NOT run.
- Automated gate: `python scripts/agent_verify.py` (checks, targeted tests, pyflakes, migrations, i18n, line limits).


## Skill: balances-and-net-worth
# Balances and net worth
- `BalanceEntry` (`core/models/balance/balance_entry.py`): owner, title, `balance_type` (cash / bank / gold / certificate), bank, currency, amount (Decimal 18,2).
- Money moves through `core/services/expenses/expense_balance_helpers.py` (`_apply_expense_balance_delta`) and the balance services in `core/services/balance/`. Never change a balance with a raw `.update()` outside these helpers.
- Net worth: `core/services/balance/net_worth_calculations.py` and `net_worth_service/`. These are financial calculations: do not change without approval.
- Cash expenses and bank expenses both reduce a matching `BalanceEntry`; a missing matching entry raises `matching_balance_entry_not_found`, too little money raises `insufficient_balance`.
- Always use `Decimal`, never `float`, for stored money. Amounts are kept in their own currency plus `amount_base` in the user's base currency (`get_user_base_code(owner)`).
- Latest exchange rates: `core/services/shared/latest_rates.latest_exchange_rates()`; never `order_by("-fetched_at").first()` inline.
- Tests: `core/tests/balance/`.


## Skill: expenses
# Expenses
- Model: `core/models/expenses.py` (`Expense`, `ExpenseCategory`, `ExpenseSubcategory`). `Expense` has owner, date, year, month, category, amount, `amount_base`, `exchange_rate`, currency, bank, payment_method (Cash / Card / Bank Transfer / Other).
- Write ONLY through `ExpenseService.create_expense / update_expense / delete_expense(…, owner)` in `core/services/expenses/expense_service.py`: they check ownership, convert currency (`CurrencyConversionService.strict_rate`) and adjust the balance in one transaction.
- Errors are `ValueError` codes: `bank_account_required`, `category_not_found`, `matching_balance_entry_not_found`, `insufficient_balance`, `readonly_mirrored_expense`, `exchange_rate_missing`.
- Rows with `source_type` set are read-only mirrors of fixed-asset records: they cannot be edited or deleted directly.
- Views: `core/views/expense_views.py`, `expense_category_views.py`, `expense_summary_views.py`. Frontend: `static/js/expenses/`.
- Tests: `core/tests/expenses/`; E2E: `tests/modules/expenses/`.


## Skill: migrations
# Migrations
- Numbered files in `core/migrations/` (`00NN_name.py`). Create with `python manage.py makemigrations core -n <name>`; check with `python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run` (must report no changes).
- Never edit or delete a migration that is already in the repo's history; add a new one. Protected by `coding_agent/config.json`.
- A new model must also be added to the backup order in `core/services/backup_serializer/export_order.py` or `core/tests/system/test_backup_coverage.py` fails.
- Data migrations must be reversible or say plainly why not. Never touch `db.sqlite3` by h

- Child rows inherit ownership through their parent (e.g. salary entries via `company__owner`).
- Start every API view with `_api_aut

example.goal: Explain what the function `build_sale_sheet` in `core/reports/fixed_asset_excel_report_generator/sale_sheet.py` does and when it is called. Answer only; do not plan or change anything.
example.answer:
build_sale_sheet(wb, lang, t, assets, header_font) creates the "Sale" worksheet of the fixed-asset Excel report. It adds a bold header row (Asset Name, Sale Date, Sale Price (base), Selling Expenses (base), Net Sale Amount, Deposit Balance, Notes — labels localized via fixed_asset_report_label), then iterates over the given assets, skips any without a sale record, and appends one row per sold asset with its name, sale date, sale price, selling expenses, net sale amount, deposit balance ID and notes (amounts coerced to float, defaults 0). It returns the worksheet object.

It is called once in core/reports/fixed_asset_excel_report_generator/generator.py (line 41), inside the GET handler of the fixed-asset Excel report API view, right after build_summary_sheet and before build_collection_sheets, after the workbook is created — i.e. whenever a user requests the fixed-asset Excel report download.

## Skill: testing
# Testing
- Django tests: `core/tests/<area>/test_*.py`; run `python manage.py test core.tests.<area>` (targeted first, then the full suite). One known sandbox-only failure: the Playwright single-page-failure-isolation test; known on main: `test_speech_api` Arabic Piper test.
- Users in tests get currencies/categories automatically: use `get_or_create`, not `create`.
- Static checks: `python -m pyflakes core tests scripts wealthflow doc_engine manage.py`, `npm run validate`, `python manage.py check`, `makemigrations --check`.
- Browser E2E: `scripts/run_full_e2e.py --headless` on the owner's PC only. Every change adds a module under `tests/modules/<name>.py`, wired in `scripts/e2e_module_dispatch.py`, `scripts/test_ui_human_full_e2e.py` and `tests/core/reporter.py` (page denominators).
- Never claim a test passed unless its command finished successfully; say plainly what was NOT run.
- Automated gate: `python scripts/agent_verify.py` (checks, targeted tests, pyflakes, migrations, i18n, line limits).


## Skill: django-architecture
# Django architecture (WealthFlow)
- Stack: Django 6 backend, vanilla-JS single-page app (no framework), SQLite in the repo (`db.sqlite3` tracked on purpose, never edit it).
- Layers: `core/models/` (one file or folder per area) -> `core/services/<area>/` (business rules) -> `core/views/` (thin JSON views) -> `core/urls/*_urls.py` (all routes `api/...`).
- Views are class-based `View`s returning `JsonResponse`. Start each handler with `_api_auth_required(request)` (from `core.validators`); body via `parse_json_body(request)`.
- Business logic belongs in a service class, never in a view. Reuse the existing service the screen already uses (e.g. `ExpenseService`) instead of writing to models directly.
- Plan gating: wrap routes with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (`core/services/billing`). Sysadmin-only views use `SysadminRequiredMixin`.
- App settings live in `AppSettings` (`AppSettings.get(key, default, user=...)`); `user=None` = global. The AI app's own `ai_*`/`speech_*`/`image_gen_*` settings live in `ai.models.AISetting` (same get/set API). Prefer a UI setting over `.env`.
- `ai/` must not import `core`: WealthFlow-specific AI code lives in `core/ai_pack` and plugs in through `settings.AI_PACKS`; host answers (admin check, audit, currency) are `AI_*` hooks in `wealthflow/settings.py` (`ai/host.py`).
- Every code file must stay <= 200 lines: split into a package folder with an `__init__.py` that re-exports.
- Shared central services are additive-only: `CurrencyConversionService`, `base_currency.py`, `ExchangeRateHistoryService`, `market_profile.py`, settings access. List every caller before touching one.


## Skill: security-and-tenancy
# Security and multi-tenancy
- Every user-owned row has an `owner` FK. Query with `Model.objects.filter(owner=request.user)` or the helpers in `core/validators/ownership.py` (`_owned_queryset`, `_owned_object_or_404`, `_child_owned_*`). No staff or superuser bypass.
- Child rows inherit ownership through their parent (e.g. salary entries via `company__owner`).
- Start every API view with `_api_auth_required(request)`. CSRF is on everywhere except the Paymob webhook. Login attempts use django-axes.
- Settings and secrets: AI provider keys are encrypted (`credential_encryption.py`); never log or return them. `.env` and `db.sqlite3` are never edited.
- Non-admins only get a whitelist from `/api/settings/`. Source-code tools of the AI are sysadmin-only.
- Every security-relevant change needs a test proving user A cannot read or change user B's data (pattern in the tests of `ai/tests/test_ai_chat_manage.py`).


## Skill: balances-and-net-worth
# Balances and net worth
- `BalanceEntry` (`core/models/balance/balance_entry.py`): owner, title, `balance_type` (cash / bank / gold / certificate), bank, currency, amount (Decimal 18,2).
- Money moves through `core/services/expenses/expense_balance_helpers.py` (`_apply_expense_balance_delta`) and the balance services in `core/services/balance/`. Never change a balance with a raw `.update()` outside these helpers.
- Net worth: `core/services/balance/net_worth_calculations.py` and `net_worth_service/`. These are financial calculations: do not change without approval.
- Cash expenses and bank expenses both reduce a matching `BalanceEntry`; a missing matching entry raises `matching_balance_entry_not_found`, too little money raises `insufficient_balance`.
- Always use `Decimal`, never `float`, for stored money. Amounts are kept in their own currency plus `amount_base` in the user's base currency (`get_user_base_code(owner)`).

- Tests: `core/tests/balance/`.

example.goal: What is `ai/doc_engine/models.py` for? List its main functions or classes with one line each. Answer only; do not plan or change anything.
example.answer:
ai/doc_engine/models.py builds the in-memory documentation tree for the app's auto-generated docs. It takes a capture manifest (pages, tabs, nested tabs, modals, screenshots) plus hand-written content (page descriptions) and assembles them into a hierarchy of DocNode objects. Main contents:

- DocNode (line 5): a single documentation node — id, title, purpose, navigation breadcrumb, steps, screenshots, children, route, is_admin.
- DocumentationModel (line 21): holds manifest + content, builds the node tree on init; exposes nodes and validation_warnings.
- DocumentationModel._auto_purpose (line 29): generates a generic purpose sentence for pages/tabs/modals lacking a hand-written description.
- DocumentationModel._get_stable_key (line 45): builds the stable route::tab::nested_tab::modal key used to look up content entries.
- DocumentationModel._build_tree (line 55): sorts pages by capture timestamp, maps each entry to a route/tab/nested-tab/modal node (creating intermediate nodes as needed) and links the final tree into self.nodes.

## Skill: django-architecture
# Django architecture (WealthFlow)
- Stack: Django 6 backend, vanilla-JS single-page app (no framework), SQLite in the repo (`db.sqlite3` tracked on purpose, never edit it).
- Layers: `core/models/` (one file or folder per area) -> `core/services/<area>/` (business rules) -> `core/views/` (thin JSON views) -> `core/urls/*_urls.py` (all routes `api/...`).
- Views are class-based `View`s returning `JsonResponse`. Start each handler with `_api_auth_required(request)` (from `core.validators`); body via `parse_json_body(request)`.
- Business logic belongs in a service class, never in a view. Reuse the existing service the screen already uses (e.g. `ExpenseService`) instead of writing to models directly.
- Plan gating: wrap routes with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (`core/services/billing`). Sysadmin-only views use `SysadminRequiredMixin`.

example.goal: Explain what the function `manifest_view` in `core/views/pwa_views.py` does and when it is called. Answer only; do not plan or change anything.
example.answer: manifest_view (core/views/pwa_views.py:31) is a GET-only Django view that serves the site's Web App Manifest. It builds a JSON dict describing the WealthFlow PWA — name/short_name, id and start_url '/', scope '/', display 'standalone', background/theme color #0a0f1e, categories ['finance','productivity'] — plus three icons (192x192, 512x512 'any', and a 512x512 'maskable' icon) resolved via static(). It returns a JsonResponse with content_type 'application/manifest+json' and Cache-Control: no-cache. It is routed at /manifest.webmanifest (core/urls/pwa_urls.py:5) and is public (no auth) because the browser fetches it without a session. It is called when a browser loads a page that references the manifest — templates/index.html:8 and templates/authentication/login.html:8 include <link rel="manifest" href="/manifest.webmanifest"> — and the browser requests it to enable installability and show app metadata (icons, display mode, theme).

example.answer: `deleteMyAccount()` (lines 68-116) is the confirm handler for the account-deletion form on the customer plans page. Step by step: 1) It reads the password and confirmation text from the form inputs (`wf-account-password`, `wf-account-confirm`), and if the confirmation text is not exactly `DELETE` it shows an error toast (`account_data_confirm_required`) and returns without doing anything. 2) It disables the confirm button, then POSTs to `/api/account/delete/` with a JSON body `{confirm, password}`, sending `Content-Type: application/json` and the `X-CSRFToken` header from `getCsrfToken()`. 3) On a successful response it shows a success toast (`account_data_deleted`) with the grace period filled in from the `grace_days` field of the JSON response, and after 1.2 s redirects the browser to `/accounts/login/`. 4) On a non-OK response it maps the server's `error` code to a user-facing message — `invalid_password` (wrong password), `last_admin` (you're the only administrator), `confirmation_required` (must type DELETE) — or falls back to a generic "Couldn't delete the account" error toast. 5) Network exceptions are caught and shown as the same generic error toast, and the button is re-enabled in the `finally` block. In short: it validates the typed DELETE confirmation, sends the password to the backend deletion endpoint, and either logs the user out after a successful scheduled deletion or displays the specific failure reason. Note the deletion is not immediate on the client side — the backend schedules it with a restore grace period.

example.answer: In `core/reports/report_generators.py`, `export_excel(request)` is a login-required function-view that builds and serves a full Balance-tracker Excel download. It lazily imports `generate_excel` from `core.reports.excel_generator`, calls `generate_excel(request.user)` to get an in-memory workbook buffer, and returns an `HttpResponse` with the XLSX MIME type and `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="Balance_Tracker_<YYYYMMDD>.xlsx"` (date via `date.today()`). It is exported in the module's `__all__` and re-exported through `core/views/exports_expense_reports.py` and `core/views/__init__.py`. Note: the only URL named `export_excel` (`/api/export/excel/` in `core/urls/settings_urls.py`) is wired to `ExportExcelWorkbookView.as_view()`, a different class — the `export_excel` function itself is not referenced by any route I could find, and `core/views/report_views.py` defines its own separate `export_excel` function. So it is a reusable view function for exporting the user's balance data as an Excel file, but in the current code it is not obviously called from any URL.

## Skill: testing
# Testing
- Django tests: `core/tests/<area>/test_*.py`; run `python manage.py test core.tests.<area>` (targeted first, then the full suite). One known sandbox-only failure: the Playwright single-page-failure-isolation test; known on main: `test_speech_api` Arabic Piper test.
- Users in tests get currencies/categories automatically: use `get_or_create`, not `create`.
- Static checks: `python -m pyflakes core tests scripts wealthflow doc_engine manage.py`, `npm run validate`, `python manage.py check`, `makemigrations --check`.
- Browser E2E: `scripts/run_full_e2e.py --headless` on the owner's PC only. Every change adds a module under `tests/modules/<name>.py`, wired in `scripts/e2e_module_dispatch.py`, `scripts/test_ui_human_full_e2e.py` and `tests/core/reporter.py` (page denominators).
- Never claim a test passed unless its command finished successfully; say plainly what was NOT run.
- Automated gate: `python scripts/agent_verify.py` (checks, targeted tests, pyflakes, migrations, i18n, line limits).


## Skill: django-architecture
# Django architecture (WealthFlow)
- Stack: Django 6 backend, vanilla-JS single-page app (no framework), SQLite in the repo (`db.sqlite3` tracked on purpose, never edit it).
- Layers: `core/models/` (one file or folder per area) -> `core/services/<area>/` (business rules) -> `core/views/` (thin JSON views) -> `core/urls/*_urls.py` (all routes `api/...`).
- Views are class-based `View`s returning `JsonResponse`. Start each handler with `_api_auth_required(request)` (from `core.validators`); body via `parse_json_body(request)`.
- Business logic belongs in a service class, never in a view. Reuse the existing service the screen already uses (e.g. `ExpenseService`) instead of writing to models directly.
- Plan gating: wrap routes with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (`core/services/billing`). Sysadmin-only views use `SysadminRequiredMixin`.
- App settings live in `AppSettings` (`AppSettings.get(key, default, user=...)`); `user=None` = global. The AI app's own `ai_*`/`speech_*`/`image_gen_*` settings live in `ai.models.AISetting` (same get/set API). Prefer a UI setting over `.env`.
- `ai/` must not import `core`: WealthFlow-specific AI code lives in `core/ai_pack` and plugs in through `settings.AI_PACKS`; host answers (admin check, audit, currency) are `AI_*` hooks in `wealthflow/settings.py` (`ai/host.py`).
- Every code file must stay <= 200 lines: split into a package folder with an `__init__.py` that re-exports.
- Shared central services are additive-only: `CurrencyConversionService`, `base_currency.py`, `ExchangeRateHistoryService`, `market_profile.py`, settings access. List every caller before touching one.


## Skill: security-and-tenancy
# Security and multi-tenancy
- Every user-owned row has an `owner` FK. Query with `Model.objects.filter(owner=request.user)` or the helpers in `core/validators/ownership.py` (`_owned_queryset`, `_owned_object_or_404`, `_child_owned_*`). No staff or superuser bypass.
- Child rows inherit ownership through their parent (e.g. salary entries via `company__owner`).
- Start every API view with `_api_auth_required(request)`. CSRF is on everywhere except the Paymob webhook. Login attempts use django-axes.
- Settings and secrets: AI provider keys are encrypted (`credential_encryption.py`); never log or return them. `.env` and `db.sqlite3` are never edited.
- Non-admins only get a whitelist from `/api/settings/`. Source-code tools of the AI are sysadmin-only.
- Every security-relevant change needs a test proving user A cannot read or change user B's data (pattern in the tests of `ai/tests/test_ai_chat_manage.py`).


## Skill: balances-and-net-worth
# Balances and net worth
- `BalanceEntry` (`core/models/balance/balance_entry.py`): owner, title, `balance_type` (cash / bank / gold / certificate), bank, currency, amount (Decimal 18,2).
- Money moves through `core/services/expenses/expense_balance_helpers.py` (`_apply_expense_balance_delta`) and the balance services in `core/services/balance/`. Never change a balance with a raw `.update()` outside these helpers.
- Net worth: `core/services/balance/net_worth_calculations.py` and `net_worth_service/`. These are financial calculations: do not change without approval.
- Cash expenses and bank expenses both reduce a matching `BalanceEntry`; a missing matching entry raises `matching_balance_entry_not_found`, too little money raises `insufficient_balance`.
- Always use `Decimal`, never `float`, for stored money. Amounts are kept in their own currency plus `amount_base` in the user's base currency (`get_user_base_code(owner)`).
- Latest exchange rates: `core/services/shared/latest_rates.latest_exchange_rates()`; never `order_by("-fetched_at").first()` inline.
- Tests: `core/tests/balance/`.


## Skill: expenses
# Expenses
- Model: `core/models/expenses.py` (`Expense`, `ExpenseCategory`, `ExpenseSubcategory`). `Expense` has owner, date, year, month, category, amount, `amount_base`, `exchange_rate`, currency, bank, payment_method (Cash / Card / Bank Transfer / Other).

## Skill: security-and-tenancy
# Security and multi-tenancy
- Every user-owned row has an `owner` FK. Query with `Model.objects.filter(owner=request.user)` or the helpers in `core/validators/ownership.py` (`_owned_queryset`, `_owned_object_or_404`, `_child_owned_*`). No staff or superuser bypass.
- Child rows inherit ownership through their parent (e.g. salary entries via `company__owner`).
- Start every API view with `_api_auth_required(request)`. CSRF is on everywhere except the Paymob webhook. Login attempts use django-axes.
- Settings and secrets: AI provider keys are encrypted (`credential_encryption.py`); never log or return them. `.env` and `db.sqlite3` are never edited.
- Non-admins only get a whitelist from `/api/settings/`. Source-code tools of the AI are sysadmin-only.
- Every security-relevant change needs a test proving user A cannot read or change user B's data (pattern in the tests of `ai/tests/test_ai_chat_manage.py`).


## Skill: testing
# Testing
- Django tests: `core/tests/<area>/test_*.py`; run `python manage.py test core.tests.<area>` (targeted first, then the full suite). One known sandbox-only failure: the Playwright single-page-failure-isolation test; known on main: `test_speech_api` Arabic Piper test.
- Users in tests get currencies/categories automatically: use `get_or_create`, not `create`.
- Static checks: `python -m pyflakes core tests scripts wealthflow doc_engine manage.py`, `npm run validate`, `python manage.py check`, `makemigrations --check`.
- Browser E2E: `scripts/run_full_e2e.py --headless` on the owner's PC only. Every change adds a module under `tests/modules/<name>.py`, wired in `scripts/e2e_module_dispatch.py`, `scripts/test_ui_human_full_e2e.py` and `tests/core/reporter.py` (page denominators).
- Never claim a test passed unless its command finished successfully; say plainly what was NOT run.
- Automated gate: `python scripts/agent_verify.py` (checks, targeted tests, pyflakes, migrations, i18n, line limits).


## Skill: django-architecture
# Django architecture (WealthFlow)
- Stack: Django 6 backend, vanilla-JS single-page app (no framework), SQLite in the repo (`db.sqlite3` tracked on purpose, never edit it).
- Layers: `core/models/` (one file or folder per area) -> `core/services/<area>/` (business rules) -> `core/views/` (thin JSON views) -> `core/urls/*_urls.py` (all routes `api/...`).
- Views are class-based `View`s returning `JsonResponse`. Start each handler with `_api_auth_required(request)` (from `core.validators`); body via `parse_json_body(request)`.
- Business logic belongs in a service class, never in a view. Reuse the existing service the screen already uses (e.g. `ExpenseService`) instead of writing to models directly.
- Plan gating: wrap routes with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (`core/services/billing`). Sysadmin-only views use `SysadminRequiredMixin`.
- App settings live in `AppSettings` (`AppSettings.get(key, default, user=...)`); `user=None` = global. The AI app's own `ai_*`/`speech_*`/`image_gen_*` settings live in `ai.models.AISetting` (same get/set API). Prefer a UI setting over `.env`.
- `ai/` must not import `core`: WealthFlow-specific AI code lives in `core/ai_pack` and plugs in through `settings.AI_PACKS`; host answers (admin check, audit, currency) are `AI_*` hooks in `wealthflow/settings.py` (`ai/host.py`).
- Every code file must stay <= 200 lines: split into a package folder with an `__init__.py` that re-exports.
- Shared central services are additive-only: `CurrencyConversionService`, `base_currency.py`, `ExchangeRateHistoryService`, `market_profile.py`, settings access. List every caller before touching one.


## Skill: balances-and-net-worth
# Balances and net worth
- `BalanceEntry` (`core/models/balance/balance_entry.py`): owner, title, `balance_type` (cash / bank / gold / certificate), bank, currency, amount (Decimal 18,2).
- Money moves through `core/services/expenses/expense_balance_helpers.py` (`_apply_expense_balance_delta`) and the balance services in `core/services/balance/`. Never change a balance with a raw `.update()` outside these helpers.
- Net worth: `core/services/balance/net_worth_calculations.py` and `net_worth_service/`. These are financial calculations: do not change without approval.
- Cash expenses and bank expenses both reduce a matching `BalanceEntry`; a missing matching entry raises `matching_balance_entry_not_found`, too little money raises `insufficient_balance`.
- Always use `Decimal`, never `float`, for stored money. Amounts are kept in their own currency plus `amount_base` in the user's base currency (`get_user_base_code(owner)`).
- Latest exchange rates: `core/services/shared/latest_rates.latest_exchange_rates()`; never `order_by("-fetched_at").first()` inline.
- Tests: `core/tests/balance/`.


## Skill: deployment
# Deployment
- Local: Windows + PowerShell, `python manage.py runserver 8000`, Ollama for the AI (`setup-ollama.bat`, guide: `WealthFlow Deployment & Ollama Setup Guide.txt`).
- Production target: PythonAnywhere (env-driven hardening in `wealthflow/settings.py`; DEBUG and tracked `.env`/`db.sqlite3` are accepted only until selling).
- Scheduled work runs through `python manage.py run_automation` (purge of deleted accounts, rates, recurring transactions): it must be scheduled in the host's Tasks.
- Payments: Paymob (test mode + regional accounts); webhook is the only CSRF-exempt endpoint.
- Never push or commit from the agent. Deliver files + `COMMIT_ME

## Skill: django-architecture

example.goal: Explain what the function `add_salary_answers` in `core/ai_pack/tools/salary_answers.py` does and when it is called. Answer only; do not plan or change anything.
example.answer:
`add_salary_answers(res, user, search_query)` in `core/ai_pack/tools/salary_answers.py` deterministically computes ready-made salary answers and prepends them to the `salary` block of the AI data-lookup result, because small local models misread long lists and yearly totals. It: (1) parses the query for a month+year (`_parse_month_year` via `ai.services.period_parser.find_periods`) and, if found, builds `requested_period_answer` by querying `SalaryEntry` rows for that owner/year/month and formatting the paid amounts in the user's primary currency (`_month_answer`); (2) if the query contains a "latest/last/recent/newest/current" word and `salary.latest_salary_entry` exists, adds `latest_paid_salary_answer` quoting its paid amount, month, year and company; (3) if the query names a year (19xx/20xx regex), adds `requested_year_entries` — every entry of that year (capped at `MAX_YEAR_ENTRIES`=120), sorted by year/month, with expected/paid/bonus formatted (`_year_entries`); and (4) replaces `res["salary"]` with `{**extra, **salary}` (a copy, so a cached dict is never mutated). It does nothing if `res["salary"]` isn't a dict.

It is called from `core/ai_pack/pack.py` in the `_salary_enricher` hook, registered via `reg.data_enrichers.append(_salary_enricher)`. `ai/services/tools/data_codebase.py` (line 90) runs every registered `data_enrichers` entry after building the data-lookup tool result, so `add_salary_answers` runs during the AI "query_application_data"/data-lookup tool flow when the result contains a `salary` dict. The same hook also appends `SALARY_INSTRUCTIONS` to `res["instructions"]` telling the model to use only these ready-made answers. It is also called directly in tests (`core/tests/ai_pack/test_query_engine_year_lists.py`).

- Layers: `core/models/` (one file or folder per area) -> `core/services/<area>/` (business rules) -> `core/views/` (thin JSON views) -> `core/urls/*_urls.py` (all routes `api/...`).
- Views are class-based `View`s returning `JsonResponse`. Start each handler with `_api_auth_required(request)` (from `core.validators`); body via `parse_json_body(request)`.
- Business logic belongs in a service class, never in a view. Reuse the existing service the screen already uses (e.g. `ExpenseService`) instead of writing to models directly.
- Plan gating: wrap routes with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (`core/services/billing`). Sysadmin-only views use `SysadminRequiredMixin`.
- App settings live in `AppSettings` (`AppSettings.get(key, default, user=...)`); `user=None` = global. The AI app's own `ai_*`/`speech_*`/`image_gen_*` settings live in `ai.models.AISetting` (same get/set API). Prefer a UI setting over `.env`.
- `ai/` must not import `core`: WealthFlow-specific AI code lives in `core/ai_pack` and plugs in through `settings.AI_PACKS`; host answers (admin check, audit, currency) are `AI_*` hooks in `wealthflow/settings.py` (`ai/host.py`).
- Every code file must stay <= 200 lines: split into a package folder with an `__init__.py` that re-exports.
- Shared central services are additive-only: `CurrencyConversionService`, `base_currency.py`, `ExchangeRateHistoryService`, `market_profile.py`, settings access. List every caller before touching one.


## Skill: security-and-tenancy
# Security and multi-tenancy
- Every user-owned row has an `owner` FK. Query with `Model.objects.filter(owner=request.user)` or the helpers in `core/validators/ownership.py` (`_owned_queryset`, `_owned_object_or_404`, `_child_owned_*`). No staff or superuser bypass.
- Child rows inherit ownership through their parent (e.g. salary entries via `company__owner`).
- Start every API view with `_api_auth_required(request)`. CSRF is on everywhere except the Paymob webhook. Login attempts use django-axes.
- Settings and secrets: AI provider keys are encrypted (`credential_encryption.py`); never log or return them. `.env` and `db.sqlite3` are never edited.
- Non-admins only get a whitelist from `/api/settings/`. Source-code tools of the AI are sysadmin-only.
- Every security-relevant change needs a test proving user A cannot read or change user B's data (pattern in the tests of `ai/tests/test_ai_chat_manage.py`).


## Skill: testing
# Testing
- Django tests: `core/tests/<area>/test_*.py`; run `python manage.py test core.tests.<area>` (targeted first, then the full suite). One known sandbox-only failure: the Playwright single-page-failure-isolation test; known on main: `test_speech_api` Arabic Piper test.
- Users in tests get currencies/categories automatically: use `get_or_create`, not `create`.
- Static checks: `python -m pyflakes core tests scripts wealthflow doc_engine manage.py`, `npm run validate`, `python manage.py check`, `makemigrations --check`.
- Browser E2E: `scripts/run_full_e2e.py --headless` on the owner's PC only. Every change adds a module under `tests/modules/<name>.py`, wired in `scripts/e2e_module_dispatch.py`, `scripts/test_ui_human_full_e2e.py` and `tests/core/reporter.py` (page denominators).
- Never claim a test passed unless its command finished successfully; say plainly what was NOT run.
- Automated gate: `python scripts/agent_verify.py` (checks, targeted tests, pyflakes, migrations, i18n, line limits).

- Money moves through `core/services/expenses/expense_balance_helpers.py` (`_apply_expense_balance_delta`) and the balance services in `core/services/balance/`. Never change a balance with a raw `.update()` outside these helpers.

- Tests: `core/tests/balance/`.

example.goal: How does the class `BadJsonError` in `ai/utils/json_body.py` work? List its methods and say what each one is for. Answer only; do not plan or change anything.
example.answer: BadJsonError (ai/utils/json_body.py, lines 13-19) is a subclass of json.JSONDecodeError used for malformed JSON request bodies. It has two methods: (1) __init__(self, message=DEFAULT_MESSAGE) — calls super().__init__(message, "", 0) with empty doc and position 0 so it behaves like a real JSONDecodeError, then stores the message on self.message (defaults to "Invalid JSON body"); (2) __str__(self) — returns self.message so the exception prints the friendly message instead of the JSONDecodeError tuple. Because it subclasses json.JSONDecodeError, existing except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) blocks still catch it, and any uncaught BadJsonError is turned into a 400 by JsonBodyErrorMiddleware (see module docstring).

example.goal: Explain what the function `parse_message` in `ai/integrations/ai_provider/ollama_response.py` does and when it is called. Answer only; do not plan or change anything.
example.answer: `parse_message(msg)` (ai/integrations/ai_provider/ollama_response.py:29) takes one message dict from an Ollama chat response and returns a `(content, tool_calls)` tuple. It does two things: (1) cleans the content with `strip_reasoning`, which removes a reasoning model's visible thinking — `<think>...</think>` blocks, everything before a lone closing `</think>` tag, and any unclosed `<think>` tail; (2) recovers tool calls the model emitted as plain JSON text instead of the proper `tool_calls` field — if the stripped content starts with `{` and mentions `function` or `name`, it tries `json.loads`, and when it's a dict with a string function name plus a dict of parameters/arguments, it converts it to the standard shape `[{"function": {"name": ..., "arguments": ...}}]` and empties the content. Non-dict inputs and failed JSON parses are returned unchanged (empty content, tool_calls as-is). It is called in exactly one place in production code: `OllamaProvider.generate()` (ai/integrations/ai_provider/ollama_provider.py:157), right after a successful non-streaming Ollama API call, to normalize `data["message"]` before building the provider result dict (`content`, `tool_calls`, token counts). It is also exercised in the unit tests ai/tests/test_ollama_reasoning_strip.py.

## Skill: testing
# Testing
- Django tests: `core/tests/<area>/test_*.py`; run `python manage.py test core.tests.<area>` (targeted first, then the full suite). One known sandbox-only failure: the Playwright single-page-failure-isolation test; known on main: `test_speech_api` Arabic Piper test.
- Users in tests get currencies/categories automatically: use `get_or_create`, not `create`.
- Static checks: `python -m pyflakes core tests scripts wealthflow doc_engine manage.py`, `npm run validate`, `python manage.py check`, `makemigrations --check`.
- Browser E2E: `scripts/run_full_e2e.py --headless` on the owner's PC only. Every change adds a module under `tests/modules/<name>.py`, wired in `scripts/e2e_module_dispatch.py`, `scripts/test_ui_human_full_e2e.py` and `tests/core/reporter.py` (page denominators).
- Never claim a test passed unless its command finished successfully; say plainly what was NOT run.
- Automated gate: `python scripts/agent_verify.py` (checks, targeted tests, pyflakes, migrations, i18n, line limits).


## Skill: django-architecture
# Django architecture (WealthFlow)
- Stack: Django 6 backend, vanilla-JS single-page app (no framework), SQLite in the repo (`db.sqlite3` tracked on purpose, never edit it).
- Layers: `core/models/` (one file or folder per area) -> `core/services/<area>/` (business rules) -> `core/views/` (thin JSON views) -> `core/urls/*_urls.py` (all routes `api/...`).
- Views are class-based `View`s returning `JsonResponse`. Start each handler with `_api_auth_required(request)` (from `core.validators`); body via `parse_json_body(request)`.
- Business logic belongs in a service class, never in a view. Reuse the existing service the screen already uses (e.g. `ExpenseService`) instead of writing to models directly.
- Plan gating: wrap routes with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (`core/services/billing`). Sysadmin-only views use `SysadminRequiredMixin`.
- App settings live in `AppSettings` (`AppSettings.get(key, default, user=...)`); `user=None` = global. The AI app's own `ai_*`/`speech_*`/`image_gen_*` settings live in `ai.models.AISetting` (same get/set API). Prefer a UI setting over `.env`.
- `ai/` must not import `core`: WealthFlow-specific AI code lives in `core/ai_pack` and plugs in through `settings.AI_PACKS`; host answers (admin check, audit, currency) are `AI_*` hooks in `wealthflow/settings.py` (`ai/host.py`).
- Every code file must stay <= 200 lines: split into a package folder with an `__init__.py` that re-exports.
- Shared central services are additive-only: `CurrencyConversionService`, `base_currency.py`, `ExchangeRateHistoryService`, `market_profile.py`, settings access. List every caller before touching one.


## Skill: security-and-tenancy
# Security and multi-tenancy
- Every user-owned row has an `owner` FK. Query with `Model.objects.filter(owner=request.user)` or the helpers in `core/validators/ownership.py` (`_owned_queryset`, `_owned_object_or_404`, `_child_owned_*`). No staff or superuser bypass.
- Child rows inherit ownership through their parent (e.g. salary entries via `company__owner`).
- Start every API view with `_api_auth_required(request)`. CSRF is on everywhere except the Paymob webhook. Login attempts use django-axes.
- Settings and secrets: AI provider keys are encrypted (`credential_encryption.py`); never log or return them. `.env` and `db.sqlite3` are never edited.
- Non-admins only get a whitelist from `/api/settings/`. Source-code tools of the AI are sysadmin-only.
- Every security-relevant change needs a test proving user A cannot read or change user B's data (pattern in the tests of `ai/tests/test_ai_chat_manage.py`).


## Skill: balances-and-net-worth
# Balances and net worth
- `BalanceEntry` (`core/models/balance/balance_entry.py`): owner, title, `balance_type` (cash / bank / gold / certificate), bank, currency, amount (Decimal 18,2).
- Money moves through `core/services/expenses/expense_balance_helpers.py` (`_apply_expense_balance_delta`) and the balance services in `core/services/balance/`. Never change a balance with a raw `.update()` outside these helpers.
- Net worth: `core/services/balance/net_worth_calculations.py` and `net_worth_service/`. These are financial calculations: do not change without approval.
- Cash expenses and bank expenses both reduce a matching `BalanceEntry`; a missing matching entry raises `matching_balance_entry_not_found`, too little money raises `insufficient_balance`.
- Always use `Decimal`, never `float`, for stored money. Amounts are kept in their own currency plus `amount_base` in the user's base currency (`get_user_base_code(owner)`).
- Latest exchange rates: `core/services/shared/latest_rates.latest_exchange_rates()`; never `order_by("-fetched_at").first()` inline.
- Tests: `core/tests/balance/`.


## Skill: deployment
# Deployment
- Local: Windows + PowerShell, `python manage.py runserver 8000`, Ollama for the AI (`setup-ollama.bat`, guide: `WealthFlow Deployment & Ollama Setup Guide.txt`).
- Production target: PythonAnywhere (env-driven hardening in `wealthflow/settings.py`; DEBUG and tracked `.env`/`db.sqlite3` are accepted only until selling).
- Scheduled work runs through `python manage.py run_automation` (purge of deleted accounts, rates, recurring transactions): it must be scheduled in the host's Tasks.
- Payments: Paymob (test mode + regional accounts); webhook is the only CSRF-exempt endpoint.
- Never push or commit from the agent. Deliver files + `COMMIT_ME

## Skill: expenses
# Expenses
- Model: `core/models/expenses.py` (`Expense`, `ExpenseCategory`, `ExpenseSubcategory`). `Expense` has owner, date, year, month, category, amount, `amount_base`, `exchange_rate`, currency, bank, payment_method (Cash / Card / Bank Transfer / Other).
- Write ONLY through `ExpenseService.create_expense / update_expense / delete_expense(…, owner)` in `core/services/expenses/expense_service.

example.answer:
ai/views/ai_speech/speech_views.py defines authenticated REST endpoints for AI speech (STT/TTS), with all provider credentials kept server-side. Main contents:

- AIWorkspaceSpeechMixin(PermissionRequiredMixin): base mixin requiring the "wealthflow_ai" permission for every speech view.
- SpeechCapabilitiesView: GET endpoint returning whether STT (speech_runtime_enabled + config enabled/configured) and TTS (tts_available) are active.
- SpeechTranscribeView: POST endpoint accepting an "audio" file (max 25 MB), calling transcribe_audio() and returning the transcribed text (404 if local speech disabled, 502 on failure).
- SpeechSynthesizeView: POST endpoint taking {"text"} (capped at 100,000 chars), returning synthesized audio via synthesize_speech() (204 if nothing speakable, 502 on failure).

It also defines MAX_SPEECH_INPUT_CHARS (100000) as a sanity cap on the TTS request body.

- Users in tests get currencies/categories automatically: use `get_or_create`, not `create`.
- Static checks: `python -m pyflakes core tests scripts wealthflow doc_engine manage.py`, `npm run validate`, `python manage.py check`, `makemigrations --check`.
- Browser E2E: `scripts/run_full_e2e.py --headless` on the owner's PC only. Every change adds a module under `tests/modules/<name>.py`, wired in `scripts/e2e_module_dispatch.py`, `scripts/test_ui_human_full_e2e.py` and `tests/core/reporter.py` (page denominators).

- Net worth: `core/services/balance/net_worth_calculations.py` and `net_worth_service/`. These are financial calculations: do not change without approval.

example.goal: Summarize the module `ai/views/mixins.py`: its purpose and its public functions. Answer only; do not plan or change anything.
example.answer:
ai/views/mixins.py (29 lines) provides class-based-view access mixins for the AI app, with the actual permission rules delegated to the host via ai.host (user_is_sysadmin, user_has_permission).

Public classes:
- SysadminRequiredMixin: extends UserPassesTestMixin; admits a request only if the user is authenticated AND user_is_sysadmin(user) is true. On denial it returns JSON: 401 {"error": "Authentication required"} for anonymous users, 403 {"error": "Admin access required"} otherwise (inherited from the private base _JsonDenied). Used for sysadmin-only AI views.
- AdminRequiredMixin: a no-op alias of SysadminRequiredMixin, kept only for backward compatibility with existing views.
- PermissionRequiredMixin: like the above but checks a single named permission; the view sets the required_key attribute and test_func returns user_has_permission(user, self.required_key). Denials use the same 401/403 JSON responses.

The only non-public name is the private base class _JsonDenied, which centralizes the JSON denial handler.

- Net worth: `core/services/balance/net_worth_calculations.py` and `net_worth_service/`. These are financial calculations: do not change without approval.

example.answer:
build_instance_kwargs(row: dict, field_map: dict, model_class, username_cache: dict[str, UserModel]) -> dict.

Parameters:
- row: the raw JSON row (dict) for one model instance; may include extra hint keys like "_content_type_label", "__<fk>__username", "__<fk>__perm", "__<fk>__group".
- field_map: mapping of field attname -> Django Field object for the model.
- model_class: the model class (accepted but actually unused in the body — only field_map drives the logic).
- username_cache: a shared dict cache mapping username -> User (or None) used to resolve User FKs without repeated queries.

Return: a dict of kwargs suitable for Model(**kwargs) or update_or_create(defaults=…), with:
- each field coerced via coerce_field(field, row.get(attname)) (dates, datetimes, decimals, binary);
- content_type_id resolved from the "_content_type_label" hint (None if the content type no longer exists);
- User FK *_id fields resolved via "__<fk>__username" hints (pk of the found User, or None if not found);
- other FKs resolved via _resolve_natural_hints using "__<fk>__perm" (app_label.model.codename, None on ValueError or Permission.DoesNotExist) or "__<fk>__group" (first matching Group pk, or None).

On bad input it degrades gracefully rather than raising: missing fields become None (row.get), unknown content types -> None, missing users -> cached None, malformed perm hints (split failure) or nonexistent Permission -> None, missing groups -> None. It does not validate the shape of row/field_map and would raise only for genuine Python errors (e.g. KeyError/TypeError from unexpected types); model_class is never touched, so an invalid model_class has no effect.

example.answer:
GoldTableParser (core/integrations/gold_price_api.py) is an html.parser.HTMLParser subclass that extracts the first on the goldbullioneg.com price page into structured rows. It keeps state flags in_table / in_tr / in_td, a current_cell dict ({"text": ..., "data_val": ...}) and a rows list of cell lists. Its methods: (1) __init__ — calls the base init and initializes in_table, in_tr, in_td, current_cell, current_row, rows. (2) handle_starttag(tag, attrs) — enters table/row/cell modes: on
sets in_table; on starts a new current_row; on appends the finished cell to current_row, appends a non-empty row to self.rows,
starts a new cell and records its data-val attribute if present. (3) handle_data(data) — appends text to the active cell's text while inside a . (4) handle_endtag(tag) — closes the current structure:
clears in_table. The parsed result is read via the public attributes parser.rows / parser.in_table etc.; there is no other public API. It is used by fetch_gold_table_prices(), which feeds the page HTML into it, then walks parser.rows expecting at least 8 rows, each with a label cell plus buy/sell cells (data_val preferred over text), classifying rows by the عيار N (karat 24/22/21/18), دولار (USD/EGP) or أونصة/ounce labels, and raising ValueError if any required price is missing.

## Skill: django-architecture
# Django architecture (WealthFlow)
- Stack: Django 6 backend, vanilla-JS single-page app (no framework), SQLite in the repo (`db.sqlite3` tracked on purpose, never edit it).
- Layers: `core/models/` (one file or folder per area) -> `core/services/<area>/` (business rules) -> `core/views/` (thin JSON views) -> `core/urls/*_urls.py` (all routes `api/...`).
- Views are class-based `View`s returning `JsonResponse`. Start each handler with `_api_auth_required(request)` (from `core.validators`); body via `parse_json_body(request)`.
- Business logic belongs in a service class, never in a view. Reuse the existing service the screen already uses (e.g. `ExpenseService`) instead of writing to models directly.
- Plan gating: wrap routes with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (`core/services/billing`). Sysadmin-only views use `SysadminRequiredMixin`.
- App settings live in `AppSettings` (`AppSettings.get(key, default, user=...)`); `user=None` = global. The AI app's own `ai_*`/`speech_*`/`image_gen_*` settings live in `ai.models.AISetting` (same get/set API). Prefer a UI setting over `.env`.
- `ai/` must not import `core`: WealthFlow-specific AI code lives in `core/ai_pack` and plugs in through `settings.AI_PACKS`; host answers (admin check, audit, currency) are `AI_*` hooks in `wealthflow/settings.py` (`ai/host.py`).
- Every code file must stay <= 200 lines: split into a package folder with an `__init__.py` that re-exports.
- Shared central services are additive-only: `CurrencyConversionService`, `base_currency.py`, `ExchangeRateHistoryService`, `market_profile.py`, settings access. List every caller before touching one.
