- Django tests: `core/tests/<area>/test_*.py`; run `python manage.py test core.tests.<area>` (targeted first, then the full suite). One known sandbox-only failure: the Playwright single-page-failure-isolation test; known on main: `test_speech_api` Arabic Piper test.
- Users in tests get currencies/categories automatically: use `get_or_create`, not `create`.
- Static checks: `python -m pyflakes core tests scripts wealthflow doc_engine manage.py`, `npm run validate`, `python manage.py check`, `makemigrations --check`.
- Browser E2E: `scripts/run_full_e2e.py --headless` on the owner's PC only. Every change adds a module under `tests/modules/<name>.py`, wired in `scripts/e2e_module_dispatch.py`, `scripts/test_ui_human_full_e2e.py` and `tests/core/reporter.py` (page denominators).

# Testing
- Django tests: `core/tests/<area>/test_*.py`; run `python manage.py test core.tests.<area>` (targeted first, then the full suite). One known sandbox-only failure: the Playwright single-page-failure-isolation test; known on main: `test_speech_api` Arabic Piper test.
- Users in tests get currencies/categories automatically: use `get_or_create`, not `create`.
- Static checks: `python -m pyflakes core tests scripts wealthflow doc_engine manage.py`, `npm run validate`, `python manage.py check`, `makemigrations --check`.
- Browser E2E: `scripts/run_full_e2e.py --headless` on the owner's PC only. Every change adds a module under `tests/modules/<name>.py`, wired in `scripts/e2e_module_dispatch.py`, `scripts/test_ui_human_full_e2e.py` and `tests/core/reporter.py` (page denominators).
- Never claim a test passed unless its command finished successfully; say plainly what was NOT run.
- Automated gate: `python scripts/agent_verify.py` (checks, targeted tests, pyflakes, migrations, i18n, line limits).


## Skill: django-architecture
# Django architecture (WealthFlow)
- Stack: Django 6 backend, vanilla-JS single-page app (no framework), SQLite in the repo (`db.sqlite3` tracked on purpose, never edit it).
- Layers: `core/models/` (one file or folder per area) -> `core/services/<area>/` (business rules) -> `core/views/` (thin JSON views) -> `core/urls/*_urls.py` (all routes `api/...`).
- Views are class-based `View`s returning `JsonResponse`. Start each handler with `_api_auth_required(request)` (from `core.validators`); body via `parse_json_body(request)`.
- Business logic belongs in a service class, never in a view. Reuse the existing service the screen already uses (e.g. `ExpenseService`) instead of writing to models directly.
- Plan gating: wrap routes with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (`core/services/billing`). Sysadmin-only views use `SysadminRequiredMixin`.
- App settings live in `AppSettings` (`AppSettings.get(key, default, user=...)`); `user=None` = global. The AI app's own `ai_*`/`speech_*`/`image_gen_*` settings live in `ai.models.AISetting` (same get/set API). Prefer a UI setting over `.env`.
- `ai/` must not import `core`: WealthFlow-specific AI code lives in `core/ai_pack` and plugs in through `settings.AI_PACKS`; host answers (admin check, audit, currency) are `AI_*` hooks in `wealthflow/settings.py` (`ai/host.py`).
- Every code file must stay <= 200 lines: split into a package folder with an `__init__.py` that re-exports.
- Shared central services are additive-only: `CurrencyConversionService`, `base_currency.py`, `ExchangeRateHistoryService`, `market_profile.py`, settings access. List every caller before touching one.


## Skill: security-and-tenancy
# Security and multi-tenancy
- Every user-owned row has an `owner` FK. Query with `Model.objects.filter(owner=request.user)` or the helpers in `core/validators/ownership.py` (`_owned_queryset`, `_owned_object_or_404`, `_child_owned_*`). No staff or superuser bypass.
- Child rows inherit ownership through their parent (e.g. salary entries via `company__owner`).
- Start every API view with `_api_auth_required(request)`. CSRF is on everywhere except the Paymob webhook. Login attempts use django-axes.
- Settings and secrets: AI provider keys are encrypted (`credential_encryption.py`); never log or return them. `.env` and `db.sqlite3` are never edited.
- Non-admins only get a whitelist from `/api/settings/`. Source-code tools of the AI are sysadmin-only.
- Every security-relevant change needs a test proving user A cannot read or change user B's data (pattern in the tests of `ai/tests/test_ai_chat_manage.py`).


## Skill: balances-and-net-worth
# Balances and net worth
- `BalanceEntry` (`core/models/balance/balance_entry.py`): owner, title, `balance_type` (cash / bank / gold / certificate), bank, currency, amount (Decimal 18,2).
- Money moves through `core/services/expenses/expense_balance_helpers.py` (`_apply_expense_balance_delta`) and the balance services in `core/services/balance/`. Never change a balance with a raw `.update()` outside these helpers.
- Net worth: `core/services/balance/net_worth_calculations.py` and `net_worth_service/`. These are financial calculations: do not change without approval.
- Cash expenses and bank expenses both reduce a matching `BalanceEntry`; a missing matching entry raises `matching_balance_entry_not_found`, too little money raises `insufficient_balance`.
- Always use `Decimal`, never `float`, for stored money. Amounts are kept in their own currency plus `amount_base` in the user's base currency (`get_user_base_code(owner)`).
- Latest exchange rates: `core/services/shared/latest_rates.latest_exchange_rates()`; never `order_by("-fetched_at").first()` inline.
- Tests: `core/tests/balance/`.


## Skill: deployment
# Deployment
- Local: Windows + PowerShell, `python manage.py runserver 8000`, Ollama for the AI (`setup-ollama.bat`, guide: `WealthFlow Deployment & Ollama Setup Guide.txt`).
- Production target: PythonAnywhere (env-driven hardening in `wealthflow/settings.py`; DEBUG and tracked `.env`/`db.sqlite3` are accepted only until selling).
- Scheduled work runs through `python manage.py run_automation` (purge of deleted accounts, rates, recurring transactions): it must be scheduled in the host's Tasks.
- Payments: Paymob (test mode + regional accounts); webhook is the only CSRF-exempt endpoint.

example.goal: What does the JavaScript function `applyTranslations` in `static/js/i18n/apply_translations.js` do? Explain it from the code. Answer only; do not plan or change anything.
example.answer:
applyTranslations(container = document) is the DOM binder for the app's i18n system. If the translation table `_t` is not loaded it returns immediately. Otherwise, within the given container (default: the whole document) it does the following, in order:

1. **Static text (`[data-i18n]`)** — replaces each element's `textContent` with `_t[key]`, skipping keys that are missing or translate to an empty string (so it never overwrites visible text with nothing).
2. **Dynamic template text (`[data-i18n-key]`)** — looks up `_t[key]` and substitutes `{placeholder}` tokens. Params come from a JSON `data-i18n-params` attribute (parsed via `parseI18nParams`, which also tries a `decodeURIComponent`'d candidate) plus convenience attributes `data-gold-amount`, `data-cash-amount`, `data-certificate-amount`, `data-days-left` (mapped to `gold_amount`, `cash_amount`, `certificate_amount`, `days_left`). `applyTemplateParams` does the `{name}` → value replacement, and `formatTemplateValue` chooses the number formatter by parameter name: integer formatting (`fmtInt`) for names matching days/count/month/year/week, plain `fmt` for ratio/trend/signal/gap/coverage/pct, otherwise `fmtpresent`; non-numeric values are inserted as strings.
3. **HTML-allowed template text (`[data-i18n-html-key]`)** — same lookup and param substitution, but writes the result with `el.innerHTML` instead of `textContent` (so markup in the translation is rendered).
4. **Prefix-based keys (`[data-i18n-prefix]` + `[data-i18n-value]`)** — concatenates prefix and raw value into a key (e.g. a payment-method code) and shows `_t[combined]`; if there's no value it shows "—", and if no translation exists it falls back to a humanized version of the raw value (underscores → spaces, words capitalized).
5. **Attributes** — `[data-i18n-placeholder]` sets the element's `placeholder` and `[data-i18n-title]` sets its `title` from the translation table.
6. **Dates** — elements with class `.local-date-field` get `textContent = formatDate(raw)` where `raw` is `data-expiry`, `data-date`, or `data-value`.
7. **Numbers** — elements with classes `.num-fmt`, `.num-fmtpresent`, `.num-fmtint`, `.num-fmtRate` render their `data-value` with `fmt`, `fmtpresent`, `fmtInt`, or `fmtRate` respectively.

Finally, if `initCollapsibleTables` exists it is called so tables rendered since the last call get their collapsible behaviour.

In short: it walks a DOM subtree and localizes all marked-up text, placeholders, titles, dates and numbers from the `_t` translation dictionary, with placeholder templating and locale-aware number/date formatting.

{"final": "applyTranslations(container = document) is the DOM binder for the app's i18n system. If the translation table `_t` is not loaded it returns immediately. Otherwise, within the given container (default: the whole document) it does the following, in order:

1. **Static text (`[data-i18n]`)** — replaces each element's `textContent` with `_t[key]`, skipping keys that are missing or translate to an empty string (so it never overwrites visible text with nothing).
2. **Dynamic template text (`[data-i18n-key]`)** — looks up `_t[key]` and substitutes `{placeholder}` tokens. Params come from a JSON `data-i18n-params` attribute (parsed via `parseI18nParams`, which also tries a `decodeURIComponent`'d candidate) plus convenience attributes `data-gold-amount`, `data-cash-amount`, `data-certificate-amount`, `data-days-left` (mapped to `gold_amount`, `cash_amount`, `certificate_amount`, `days_left`). `applyTemplateParams` does the `{name}` → value replacement, and `formatTemplateValue` chooses the number formatter by parameter name: integer formatting (`fmtInt`) for names matching days/count/month/year/week, plain `fmt` for ratio/trend/signal/gap/coverage/pct, otherwise `fmtpresent`; non-numeric values are inserted as strings.
3. **HTML-allowed template text (`[data-i18n-html-key]`)** — same lookup and param substitution, but writes the result with `el.innerHTML` instead of `textContent` (so markup in the translation is rendered).
4. **Prefix-based keys (`[data-i18n-prefix]` + `[data-i18n-value]`)** — concatenates prefix and raw value into a key (e.g. a payment-method code) and shows `_t[combined]`; if there's no value it shows "—", and if no translation exists it falls back to a humanized version of the raw value (underscores → spaces, words capitalized).
5. **Attributes** — `[data-i18n-placeholder]` sets the element's `placeholder` and `[data-i18n-title]` sets its `title` from the translation table.
6. **Dates** — elements with class `.local-date-field` get `textContent = formatDate(raw)` where `raw` is `data-expiry`, `data-date`, or `data-value`.
7. **Numbers** — elements with classes `.num-fmt`, `.num-fmtpresent`, `.num-fmtint`, `.num-fmtRate` render their `data-value` with `fmt`, `fmtpresent`, `fmtInt`, or `fmtRate` respectively.

Finally, if `initCollapsibleTables` exists it is called so tables rendered since the last call get their collapsible behaviour.

## Skill: django-architecture
# Django architecture (WealthFlow)
- Stack: Django 6 backend, vanilla-JS single-page app (no framework), SQLite in the repo (`db.sqlite3` tracked on purpose, never edit it).
- Layers: `core/models/` (one file or folder per area) -> `core/services/<area>/` (business rules) -> `core/views/` (thin JSON views) -> `core/urls/*_urls.py` (all routes `api/...`).
- Views are class-based `View`s returning `JsonResponse`. Start each handler with `_api_auth_required(request)` (from `core.validators`); body via `parse_json_body(request)`.
- Business logic belongs in a service class, never in a view. Reuse the existing service the screen already uses (e.g. `ExpenseService`) instead of writing to models directly.
- Plan gating: wrap routes with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (`core/services/billing`). Sysadmin-only views use `SysadminRequiredMixin`.
- App settings live in `AppSettings` (`AppSettings.get(key, default, user=...)`); `user=None` = global. The AI app's own `ai_*`/`speech_*`/`image_gen_*` settings live in `ai.models.AISetting` (same get/set API). Prefer a UI setting over `.env`.
- `ai/` must not import `core`: WealthFlow-specific AI code lives in `core/ai_pack` and plugs in through `settings.AI_PACKS`; host answers (admin check, audit, currency) are `AI_*` hooks in `wealthflow/settings.py` (`ai/host.py`).
- Every code file must stay <= 200 lines: split into a package folder with an `__init__.py` that re-exports.
- Shared central services are additive-only: `CurrencyConversionService`, `base_currency.py`, `ExchangeRateHistoryService`, `market_profile.py`, settings access. List every caller before touching one.

example.answer: BaseHistoricalRateProvider (core/integrations/historical_exchange_rate_provider/records.py) is an ABC defining the interface ExchangeRateHistoryService uses to pull historical FX data from any source. Class attribute: SOURCE_NAME (str, defaults to 'unknown') — identifies the provider. Methods: (1) fetch_date(target_date) -> list[HistoricalRateRecord] — abstract; a subclass must implement it to return all known currency rates for that date, an empty list if no data, and it must never raise (log errors and return []). (2) fetch_range(start, end) -> dict[date, list[HistoricalRateRecord]] — concrete helper that iterates day by day over [start, end], calling fetch_date for each date and collecting results into a dict keyed by date; subclasses can override it for efficiency. It returns HistoricalRateRecord value objects (currency_code, currency_name, buy_rate, sell_rate, mid_rate, source, snapshot_date; all rates are Decimal).

example.answer: exportExpenses() builds and downloads a CSV export of the user's expenses. Steps: (1) It reads the year and month filter values from the page inputs `fYear` and `fMonth` (optional). (2) It fetches the matching expenses from the API endpoint `/api/expenses/`, appending `year=` and/or `month=` query params, and parses the JSON response. (3) It creates a header row with columns Date, Category, Subcategory, Description, Method, Amount, Notes — using the global `t()` translation function when available (falling back to the English words). (4) For each entry in `data.entries`, it builds a row: `formatDate(e.date)`, the category/subcategory/payment-method names (each passed through `t(name, name)` for translation when `t` exists), `e.description`, `e.amount`, and `e.notes`, defaulting missing values to empty strings. (5) It serializes all rows to CSV, quoting every cell and doubling embedded quotes (`"` → `""`), joined with commas and CRLF line breaks. (6) It prepends a UTF-8 BOM (\ufeff) so MS Excel opens Arabic/UTF-8 text correctly, wraps the string in a Blob of type `text/csv;charset=utf-8`, and triggers a download via a temporary `<a>` element whose filename is `expenses_<year|all>_<month|all>.csv`. (7) Finally it calls `showToast` with a success message ("CSV exported ✓", translated if `t` is available).

example.answer: `copy_legacy_settings` (ai/legacy.py) is a one-time migration helper that copies host settings stored in a legacy key/value table into the AI app's `AISetting` model. It reads the `AI_LEGACY_SETTINGS_MODEL` setting ("app_label.Model"); if unset it returns 0. It then guards against running before the target table exists (checks the table via introspection) and skips if the marker row `ai_legacy_settings_copied` already exists. It loads all rows (key, value, description, owner_id) from the legacy model, and for each row whose key starts with one of the configured prefixes (default `ai_`, `speech_`, `image_gen_`), it runs `get_or_create` on `AISetting` — so existing AISetting rows win and are never overwritten. It finally creates the marker row so the copy runs only once, and returns the number of newly created rows. Any failure to load the legacy model/table is swallowed and returns 0 so a later migrate can retry. A `post_migrate_copy` hook wires it to run automatically after the `ai` app is migrated. Old rows are never modified or deleted.

example.answer: `resolve_domain(requested="")` in `ai/services/domains.py` decides which chat domain an AI question runs in. It reads the sysadmin-enabled domains via `enabled_domains()` (the two domains are `business_data_analysis` and `app_features_architecture`, toggled by the `ai_domain_business` / `ai_domain_app` AISettings, both on by default and at least one always stays on). ## Skill: django-architecture
# Django architecture (WealthFlow)
- Stack: Django 6 backend, vanilla-JS single-page app (no framework), SQLite in the repo (`db.sqlite3` tracked on purpose, never edit it).
- Layers: `core/models/` (one file or folder per area) -> `core/services/<area>/` (business rules) -> `core/views/` (thin JSON views) -> `core/urls/*_urls.py` (all routes `api/...`).
- Views are class-based `View`s returning `JsonResponse`. Start each handler with `_api_auth_required(request)` (from `core.validators`); body via `parse_json_body(request)`.
- Business logic belongs in a service class, never in a view. Reuse the existing service the screen already uses (e.g. `ExpenseService`) instead of writing to models directly.
- Plan gating: wrap routes with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (`core/services/billing`). Sysadmin-only views use `SysadminRequiredMixin`.
- App settings live in `AppSettings` (`AppSettings.get(key, default, user=...)`); `user=None` = global. The AI app's own `ai_*`/`speech_*`/`image_gen_*` settings live in `ai.models.AISetting` (same get/set API). Prefer a UI setting over `.env`.
- `ai/` must not import `core`: WealthFlow-specific AI code lives in `core/ai_pack` and plugs in through `settings.AI_PACKS`; host answers (admin check, audit, currency) are `AI_*` hooks in `wealthflow/settings.py` (`ai/host.py`).
- Every code file must stay <= 200 lines: split into a package folder with an `__init__.py` that re-exports.
- Shared central services are additive-only: `CurrencyConversionService`, `base_currency.py`, `ExchangeRateHistoryService`, `market_profile.py`, settings access. List every caller before touching one.

- Static checks: `python -m pyflakes core tests scripts wealthflow doc_engine manage.py`, `npm run validate`, `python manage.py check`, `makemigrations --check`.

example.answer:
ai/views/ai_prompt_views.py provides the REST API for managing AI prompts (a prompt library). It is a thin Django view layer that delegates all business logic to AIPromptService (ai.services). Its contents:
- _api_auth_required(request): returns a 401 JsonResponse if the user is not authenticated.
- AIPromptListView: GET lists/searches/prompts paginated (filters by category, search, favorites, sort) and POST creates a new prompt.
- AIPromptDetailView: GET retrieves one prompt by pk, PUT updates it, DELETE removes it.
- AIPromptFavoriteView: POST toggles the favorite flag on a prompt.
- AIPromptUseView: POST records a usage event for a prompt.
- AIPromptDuplicateView: POST duplicates an existing prompt (returns 201 with the copy).
- AIPromptCategoryListView: GET returns the list of prompt categories.

## Skill: testing
# Testing
- Django tests: `core/tests/<area>/test_*.py`; run `python manage.py test core.tests.<area>` (targeted first, then the full suite). One known sandbox-only failure: the Playwright single-page-failure-isolation test; known on main: `test_speech_api` Arabic Piper test.
- Users in tests get currencies/categories automatically: use `get_or_create`, not `create`.
- Static checks: `python -m pyflakes core tests scripts wealthflow doc_engine manage.py`, `npm run validate`, `python manage.py check`, `makemigrations --check`.
- Browser E2E: `scripts/run_full_e2e.py --headless` on the owner's PC only. Every change adds a module under `tests/modules/<name>.py`, wired in `scripts/e2e_module_dispatch.py`, `scripts/test_ui_human_full_e2e.py` and `tests/core/reporter.py` (page denominators).
- Never claim a test passed unless its command finished successfully; say plainly what was NOT run.
- Automated gate: `python scripts/agent_verify.py` (checks, targeted tests, pyflakes, migrations, i18n, line limits).


## Skill: django-architecture
# Django architecture (WealthFlow)
- Stack: Django 6 backend, vanilla-JS single-page app (no framework), SQLite in the repo (`db.sqlite3` tracked on purpose, never edit it).
- Layers: `core/models/` (one file or folder per area) -> `core/services/<area>/` (business rules) -> `core/views/` (thin JSON views) -> `core/urls/*_urls.py` (all routes `api/...`).
- Views are class-based `View`s returning `JsonResponse`. Start each handler with `_api_auth_required(request)` (from `core.validators`); body via `parse_json_body(request)`.
- Business logic belongs in a service class, never in a view. Reuse the existing service the screen already uses (e.g. `ExpenseService`) instead of writing to models directly.
- Plan gating: wrap routes with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (`core/services/billing`). Sysadmin-only views use `SysadminRequiredMixin`.
- App settings live in `AppSettings` (`AppSettings.get(key, default, user=...)`); `user=None` = global. The AI app's own `ai_*`/`speech_*`/`image_gen_*` settings live in `ai.models.AISetting` (same get/set API). Prefer a UI setting over `.env`.
- `ai/` must not import `core`: WealthFlow-specific AI code lives in `core/ai_pack` and plugs in through `settings.AI_PACKS`; host answers (admin check, audit, currency) are `AI_*` hooks in `wealthflow/settings.py` (`ai/host.py`).
- Every code file must stay <= 200 lines: split into a package folder with an `__init__.py` that re-exports.
- Shared central services are additive-only: `CurrencyConversionService`, `base_currency.py`, `ExchangeRateHistoryService`, `market_profile.py`, settings access. List every caller before touching one.


## Skill: frontend
# Frontend
- Vanilla JS, one file per concern under `static/js/<area>/`, <= 200 lines each. No bundler: scripts are loaded in order from `templates/partials/scripts/0N_*.html` (AI workspace = `04_ai.html`). Line order is load order.
- Every changed JS/CSS file needs its `?v=` number bumped in the template that includes it (browsers cache by that number). A new file needs a new `<script>` / `@import` line.
- Text shown to users comes from `_aiT(key, fallback)` / `t(key, fallback)` or `data-i18n` attributes; never hardcode a visible string.
- Escape every inserted value with `_escapeHtml`. Use `fetch` with the `X-CSRFToken` header from `window.wfGetCsrfToken()` for POST/PATCH/DELETE.
- Extension hook for chat bubbles: push a function to `window._aiMessageExtras` (receives `{role, content, toolCalls, messageId}`, returns HTML).
- Checks: `node --check <file>`, `npm run validate`, `npm run format` (ESLint config `config/linting/.eslintrc.json`, htmlhint, stylelint, prettier).
- Arabic is RTL: use logical CSS (`margin-inline-start`, `inset-inline-end`).


## Skill: expenses
# Expenses
- Model: `core/models/expenses.py` (`Expense`, `ExpenseCategory`, `ExpenseSubcategory`). `Expense` has owner, date, year, month, category, amount, `amount_base`, `exchange_rate`, currency, bank, payment_method (Cash / Card / Bank Transfer / Other).
- Write ONLY through `ExpenseService.create_expense / update_expense / delete_expense(…, owner)` in `core/services/expenses/expense_service.py`: they check ownership, convert currency (`CurrencyConversionService.strict_rate`) and adjust the balance in one transaction.
- Errors are `ValueError` codes: `bank_account_required`, `category_not_found`, `matching_balance_entry_not_found`, `insufficient_balance`, `readonly_mirrored_expense`, `exchange_rate_missing`.
- Rows with `source_type` set are read-only mirrors of fixed-asset records: they cannot be edited or deleted directly.
- Views: `core/views/expense_views.py`, `expense_category_views.py`, `expense_summary_views.py`. Frontend: `static/js/expenses/`.
- Tests: `core/tests/expenses/`; E2E: `tests/modules/expenses/`.

- Numbered files in `core/migrations/` (`00NN_name.py`). Create with `python manage.py makemigrations core -n <name>`; check with `python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run` (must report no changes).

## Skill: testing
# Testing
- Django tests: `core/tests/<area>/test_*.py`; run `python manage.py test core.tests.<area>` (targeted first, then the full suite). One known sandbox-only failure: the Playwright single-page-failure-isolation test; known on main: `test_speech_api` Arabic Piper test.
- Users in tests get currencies/categories automatically: use `get_or_create`, not `create`.
- Static checks: `python -m pyflakes core tests scripts wealthflow doc_engine manage.py`, `npm run validate`, `python manage.py check`, `makemigrations --check`.
- Browser E2E: `scripts/run_full_e2e.py --headless` on the owner's PC only. Every change adds a module under `tests/modules/<name>.py`, wired in `scripts/e2e_module_dispatch.py`, `scripts/test_ui_human_full_e2e.py` and `tests/core/reporter.py` (page denominators).
- Never claim a test passed unless its command finished successfully; say plainly what was NOT run.
- Automated gate: `python scripts/agent_verify.py` (checks, targeted tests, pyflakes, migrations, i18n, line limits).


## Skill: django-architecture
# Django architecture (WealthFlow)
- Stack: Django 6 backend, vanilla-JS single-page app (no framework), SQLite in the repo (`db.sqlite3` tracked on purpose, never edit it).
- Layers: `core/models/` (one file or folder per area) -> `core/services/<area>/` (business rules) -> `core/views/` (thin JSON views) -> `core/urls/*_urls.py` (all routes `api/...`).
- Views are class-based `View`s returning `JsonResponse`. Start each handler with `_api_auth_required(request)` (from `core.validators`); body via `parse_json_body(request)`.
- Business logic belongs in a service class, never in a view. Reuse the existing service the screen already uses (e.g. `ExpenseService`) instead of writing to models directly.
- Plan gating: wrap routes with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (`core/services/billing`). Sysadmin-only views use `SysadminRequiredMixin`.
- App settings live in `AppSettings` (`AppSettings.get(key, default, user=...)`); `user=None` = global. The AI app's own `ai_*`/`speech_*`/`image_gen_*` settings live in `ai.models.AISetting` (same get/set API). Prefer a UI setting over `.env`.
- `ai/` must not import `core`: WealthFlow-specific AI code lives in `core/ai_pack` and plugs in through `settings.AI_PACKS`; host answers (admin check, audit, currency) are `AI_*` hooks in `wealthflow/settings.py` (`ai/host.py`).
- Every code file must stay <= 200 lines: split into a package folder with an `__init__.py` that re-exports.
- Shared central services are additive-only: `CurrencyConversionService`, `base_currency.py`, `ExchangeRateHistoryService`, `market_profile.py`, settings access. List every caller before touching one.


## Skill: expenses
# Expenses
- Model: `core/models/expenses.py` (`Expense`, `ExpenseCategory`, `ExpenseSubcategory`). `Expense` has owner, date, year, month, category, amount, `amount_base`, `exchange_rate`, currency, bank, payment_method (Cash / Card / Bank Transfer / Other).
- Write ONLY through `ExpenseService.create_expense / update_expense / delete_expense(…, owner)` in `core/services/expenses/expense_service.py`: they check ownership, convert currency (`CurrencyConversionService.strict_rate`) and adjust the balance in one transaction.
- Errors are `ValueError` codes: `bank_account_required`, `category_not_found`, `matching_balance_entry_not_found`, `insufficient_balance`, `readonly_mirrored_expense`, `exchange_rate_missing`.
- Rows with `source_type` set are read-only mirrors of fixed-asset records: they cannot be edited or deleted directly.
- Views: `core/views/expense_views.py`, `expense_category_views.py`, `expense_summary_views.py`. Frontend: `static/js/expenses/`.
- Tests: `core/tests/expenses/`; E2E: `tests/modules/expenses/`.


## Skill: frontend
# Frontend
- Vanilla JS, one file per concern under `static/js/<area>/`, <= 200 lines each. No bundler: scripts are loaded in order from `templates/partials/scripts/0N_*.html` (AI workspace = `04_ai.html`). Line order is load order.
- Every changed JS/CSS file needs its `?v=` number bumped in the template that includes it (browsers cache by that number). A new file needs a new `<script>` / `@import` line.
- Text shown to users comes from `_aiT(key, fallback)` / `t(key, fallback)` or `data-i18n` attributes; never hardcode a visible string.
- Escape every inserted value with `_escapeHtml`. Use `fetch` with the `X-CSRFToken` header from `window.wfGetCsrfToken()` for POST/PATCH/DELETE.
- Extension hook for chat bubbles: push a function to `window._aiMessageExtras` (receives `{role, content, toolCalls, messageId}`, returns HTML).
- Checks: `node --check <file>`, `npm run validate`, `npm run format` (ESLint config `config/linting/.eslintrc.json`, htmlhint, stylelint, prettier).
- Arabic is RTL: use logical CSS (`margin-inline-start`, `inset-inline-end`).


## Skill: migrations
# Migrations
- Numbered files in `core/migrations/` (`00NN_name.py`). Create with `python manage.py makemigrations core -n <name>`; check with `python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run` (must report no changes).
- Never edit or delete a migration that is already in the repo's history; add a new one. Protected by `coding_agent/config.json`.
- A new model must also be added to the backup order in `core/services/backup_serializer/export_order.py` or `core/tests/system/test_backup_coverage.py` fails.
- Data migrations must be reversible or say plainly why not. Never touch `db.sqlite3` by hand.

## Skill: testing
# Testing
- Django tests: `core/tests/<area>/test_*.py`; run `python manage.py test core.tests.<area>` (targeted first, then the full suite). One known sandbox-only failure: the Playwright single-page-failure-isolation test; known on main: `test_speech_api` Arabic Piper test.

- Static checks: `python -m pyflakes core tests scripts wealthflow doc_engine manage.py`, `npm run validate`, `python manage.py check`, `makemigrations --check`.
- Browser E2E: `scripts/run_full_e2e.py --headless` on the owner's PC only. Every change adds a module under `tests/modules/<name>.py`, wired in `scripts/e2e_module_dispatch.py`, `scripts/test_ui_human_full_e2e.py` and `tests/core/reporter.py` (page denominators).

- Errors are `ValueError` codes: `bank_account_required`, `category_not_found`, `matching_balance_entry_not_found`, `insufficient_balance`, `readonly_mirrored_expense`, `exchange_rate_missing`.

## Skill: security-and-tenancy
# Security and multi-tenancy
- Every user-owned row has an `owner` FK. Query with `Model.objects.filter(owner=request.user)` or the helpers in `core/validators/ownership.py` (`_owned_queryset`, `_owned_object_or_404`, `_child_owned_*`). No staff or superuser bypass.
- Child rows inherit ownership through their parent (e.g. salary entries via `company__owner`).
- Start every API view with `_api_auth_required(request)`. CSRF is on everywhere except the Paymob webhook. Login attempts use django-axes.
- Settings and secrets: AI provider keys are encrypted (`credential_encryption.py`); never log or return them. `.env` and `db.sqlite3` are never edited.
- Non-admins only get a whitelist from `/api/settings/`. Source-code tools of the AI are sysadmin-only.

- Stack: Django 6 backend, vanilla-JS single-page app (no framework), SQLite in the repo (`db.sqlite3` tracked on purpose, never edit it).

example.goal: What does `semantic_scores` in `ai/services/retrieval/embeddings.py` do? Explain it from the code. Answer only; do not plan or change anything.
example.answer:
`semantic_scores(query, candidates)` (ai/services/retrieval/embeddings.py:112) computes cosine-similarity scores between a user query and a set of candidate texts, as a bonus retrieval signal alongside keyword scoring.

How it works:
1. It embeds the query via `_embed_query`, which first checks a 32-entry LRU (`_query_cache`) so repeated embeds of the same query in one turn (provider scoring + advisor-service scoring) don't cost another Ollama call. A miss calls `_embed`, which POSTs `{model, prompt}` to Ollama's `/api/embeddings` (URL and model from `AISetting`, defaults `http://localhost:11434` / `nomic-embed-text`, 5s timeout). `_embed` never raises: on any failure it sets a 120s circuit-breaker cooldown (`_failed_until`), logs, and returns None.
2. For each candidate `{key: description}`, it looks up a persistent module-level `_candidate_cache` (the candidate set — provider/service descriptions — doesn't change at runtime), embedding and caching the description on first use.
3. It scores each candidate with `_cosine` (dot product over the product of norms; 0.0 on length mismatch or zero vectors) and clamps to `max(0.0, ...)`, so the result is a dict `{key: similarity in [0,1]}`.

If the query embedding fails (service down, model not pulled, timeout, cooldown active) or any candidate embedding fails, it returns `None`; per the docstring the caller then falls back to keyword-only scoring, so an embedding outage degrades gracefully instead of breaking retrieval. Module-level `stats` counters (calls, failures, ms, cache hits, skips) and `stats_snapshot`/`stats_delta` let the pipeline trace report time spent here.

example.answer:
ai/migrations_support.py (80 lines) provides helpers for the ai app's initial migration (ai/migrations/0001_initial) so it works whether or not the host project already created the AI tables. Its purpose: make the ai app's migration idempotent and preserve existing ContentType rows.

Contents:
- Constants: NEW_LABEL = "ai" and MODELS (the 9 ai model names).
- _legacy(): reads optional host hooks from settings, AI_LEGACY_APP_LABEL (old ContentType app label) and AI_LEGACY_CREATOR_NODES (host migration nodes that already create the AI tables); both unset on a fresh host.
- _core_history_creates_tables(connection): checks the migration graph to see if another chain will create the tables.
- CreateModelIfMissing: a subclass of migrations.CreateModel whose database_forwards skips table creation if the table already exists or core will create it, and whose database_backwards is a no-op (never drops data on reversal).
- _assigned(apps, db, ct_row): True if any permission of a ContentType row is granted to a group or user.
- _relabel(apps, schema_editor, src, dst): moves ContentType rows from src to dst, keeping the oldest id and deleting unassigned duplicates (skips if django_content_type is absent or a duplicate is assigned).

Public entry points used by the migration: the CreateModelIfMissing class, and the run Python functions relabel_forward(apps, schema_editor) and relabel_backward(apps, schema_editor), which relabel ContentType rows between the legacy label and "ai" (no-op when no legacy label is set). The _-prefixed functions are internal helpers.

## `AzureOpenAIProvider` — how it works

**Class:** `ai/integrations/azure_openai_provider/__init__.py` (lines 33–167)

**Inheritance:** `AzureOpenAIConfigMixin` (from `config.py`) + `BaseAIProvider`

**Key attributes:**
- `PROVIDER_NAME = "azure"`
- `supports_tools = True`

All HTTP calls go through `make_json_http_request` (stdlib `urllib`-based), so no `requests` dependency. Secrets (the API key) are always passed into a `secrets` list and redacted from any error text via `redact_secrets`.

---

### Methods

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **`__init__(api_key, endpoint, deployment, api_version, timeout)`** | Stores and normalises the four Azure connection parameters. Strips whitespace, rstrips trailing `/` from the endpoint, defaults `api_version` to `"2024-06-01"`, and clamps `timeout` to at least 1 second. |
| **`generate(messages, tools=None, **kwargs)`** | The main chat-completion call. Validates that `api_key`, `endpoint`, and `deployment` are set (returns an error dict if not). Builds the URL `…/openai/deployments/<deployment>/chat/completions?api-version=…`, sends a POST with `api-key` header and a JSON body of `messages` (+ optional `tools`). Returns a dict with `content`, `tool_calls`, `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, and `error`. On HTTP failure or malformed response, returns an empty-content dict with a redacted `error` string. |
| **`check_connection()`** | Lightweight connectivity test. GETs `…/openai/deployments?api-version=…` and returns `{reachable, version, error, response_time_ms}`. No deployment name is required — it only checks that the API key and endpoint respond. |
| **`list_models()`** | GETs the same deployments list endpoint and extracts each item's `id` into a list of `{"name": id, "model": id}`. If the request fails or returns no data, falls back to returning the single configured `deployment` (if set) or an empty list. |
| **`check_model_available(model)`** | Quick availability check. Compares the requested `model` (or falls back to `self.deployment`) against a non-empty string, then simply verifies that `api_key` and `endpoint` are both set. Returns `True`/`False`. It does **not** make a network call — it's a config-presence check. |

---

### Summary of design
- **Deployment-based, not model-based:** Azure OpenAI requires a *deployment* name; the class treats it as the primary identifier.
- **No external HTTP library:** uses the shared `make_json_http_request` helper.
- **Secret safety:** the API key is never logged or returned; `redact_secrets` scrubs it from any error string before it reaches the caller.
- **Graceful degradation:** every method handles the "not configured" case by returning an empty/error structure rather than raising.
- **Package split (200-line rule):** config/schema logic lives in `config.py` (`AzureOpenAIConfigMixin`); the provider class stays in `__init__.py` because tests patch `make_json_http_request` in this module's namespace.

## Skill: django-architecture
# Django architecture (WealthFlow)
- Stack: Django 6 backend, vanilla-JS single-page app (no framework), SQLite in the repo (`db.sqlite3` tracked on purpose, never edit it).
- Layers: `core/models/` (one file or folder per area) -> `core/services/<area>/` (business rules) -> `core/views/` (thin JSON views) -> `core/urls/*_urls.py` (all routes `api/...`).

- Business logic belongs in a service class, never in a view. Reuse the existing service the screen already uses (e.g. `ExpenseService`) instead of writing to models directly.
- Plan gating: wrap routes with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (`core/services/billing`). Sysadmin-only views use `SysadminRequiredMixin`.
- App settings live in `AppSettings` (`AppSettings.get(key, default, user=...)`); `user=None` = global. The AI app's own `ai_*`/`speech_*`/`image_gen_*` settings live in `ai.models.AISetting` (same get/set API). Prefer a UI setting over `.env`.

{"final": "## `AzureOpenAIProvider` — how it works

**Class:** `ai/integrations/azure_openai_provider/__init__.py` (lines 33–167)

**Inheritance:** `AzureOpenAIConfigMixin` (from `config.py`) + `BaseAIProvider`

**Key attributes:**
- `PROVIDER_NAME = "azure"`
- `supports_tools = True`

All HTTP calls go through `make_json_http_request` (stdlib `urllib`-based), so no `requests` dependency. Secrets (the API key) are always passed into a `secrets` list and redacted from any error text via `redact_secrets`.

---

### Methods

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **`__init__(api_key, endpoint, deployment, api_version, timeout)`** | Stores and normalises the four Azure connection parameters. Strips whitespace, rstrips trailing `/` from the endpoint, defaults `api_version` to `"2024-06-01"`, and clamps `timeout` to at least 1 second. |
| **`generate(messages, tools=None, **kwargs)`** | The main chat-completion call. Validates that `api_key`, `endpoint`, and `deployment` are set (returns an error dict if not). Builds the URL `…/openai/deployments/<deployment>/chat/completions?api-version=…`, sends a POST with `api-key` header and a JSON body of `messages` (+ optional `tools`). Returns a dict with `content`, `tool_calls`, `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, and `error`. On HTTP failure or malformed response, returns an empty-content dict with a redacted `error` string. |
| **`check_connection()`** | Lightweight connectivity test. GETs `…/openai/deployments?api-version=…` and returns `{reachable, version, error, response_time_ms}`. No deployment name is required — it only checks that the API key and endpoint respond. |
| **`list_models()`** | GETs the same deployments list endpoint and extracts each item's `id` into a list of `{"name": id, "model": id}`. If the request fails or returns no data, falls back to returning the single configured `deployment` (if set) or an empty list. |
| **`check_model_available(model)`** | Quick availability check. Compares the requested `model` (or falls back to `self.deployment`) against a non-empty string, then simply verifies that `api_key` and `endpoint` are both set. Returns `True`/`False`. It does **not** make a network call — it's a config-presence check. |

---

### Summary of design
- **Deployment-based, not model-based:** Azure OpenAI requires a *deployment* name; the class treats it as the primary identifier.
- **No external HTTP library:** uses the shared `make_json_http_request` helper.
- **Secret safety:** the API key is never logged or returned; `redact_secrets` scrubs it from any error string before it reaches the caller.
- **Graceful degradation:** every method handles the "not configured" case by returning an empty/error structure rather than raising.
- **Package split (200-line rule):** config/schema logic lives in `config.py` (`AzureOpenAIConfigMixin`); the provider class stays in `__init__.py` because tests patch `make_json_http_request` in this module's namespace."}

## Skill: django-architecture
# Django architecture (WealthFlow)
- Stack: Django 6 backend, vanilla-JS single-page app (no framework), SQLite in the repo (`db.sqlite3` tracked on purpose, never edit it).
- Layers: `core/models/` (one file or folder per area) -> `core/services/<area>/` (business rules) -> `core/views/` (thin JSON views) -> `core/urls/*_urls.py` (all routes `api/...`).

- Business logic belongs in a service class, never in a view. Reuse the existing service the screen already uses (e.g. `ExpenseService`) instead of writing to models directly.
- Plan gating: wrap routes with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (`core/services/billing`). Sysadmin-only views use `SysadminRequiredMixin`.
- App settings live in `AppSettings` (`AppSettings.get(key, default, user=...)`); `user=None` = global. The AI app's own `ai_*`/`speech_*`/`image_gen_*` settings live in `ai.models.AISetting` (same get/set API). Prefer a UI setting over `.env`.

# Security and multi-tenancy

- Child rows inherit ownership through their parent (e.g. salary entries via `company__owner`).
- Start every API view with `_api_auth_required(request)`. CSRF is on everywhere except the Paymob webhook. Login attempts use django-axes.
- Settings and secrets: AI provider keys are encrypted (`credential_encryption.py`); never log or return them. `.env` and `db.sqlite3` are never edited.
- Non-admins only get a whitelist from `/api/settings/`. Source-code tools of the AI are sysadmin-only.
- Every security-relevant change needs a test proving user A cannot read or change user B's data (pattern in the tests of `ai/tests/test_ai_chat_manage.py`).

34	        return ""
35	
36	    context_blocks: list[str] = []
37	    current_chars = len(HEADER)
38	    max_chars = token_limit * 4

51	            current_chars += len(block)
52	            continue
53

## Skill: django-architecture
# Django architecture (WealthFlow)
- Stack: Django 6 backend, vanilla-JS single-page app (no framework), SQLite in the repo (`db.sqlite3` tracked on purpose, never edit it).
- Layers: `core/models/` (one file or folder per area) -> `core/services/<area>/` (business rules) -> `core/views/` (thin JSON views) -> `core/urls/*_urls.py` (all routes `api/...`).
- Views are class-based `View`s returning `JsonResponse`. Start each handler with `_api_auth_required(request)` (from `core.validators`); body via `parse_json_body(request)`.

- Plan gating: wrap routes with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (`core/services/billing`). Sysadmin-only views use `SysadminRequiredMixin`.
- App settings live in `AppSettings` (`AppSettings.get(key, default, user=...)`); `user=None` = global. The AI app's own `ai_*`/`speech_*`/`image_gen_*` settings live in `ai.models.AISetting` (same get/set API). Prefer a UI setting over `.env`.

- Every code file must stay <= 200 lines: split into a package folder with an `__init__.py` that re-exports.
- Shared central services are additive-only: `CurrencyConversionService`, `base_currency.py`, `ExchangeRateHistoryService`, `market_profile.py`, settings access. List every caller before touching one.


## Skill: security-and-tenancy
# Security and multi-tenancy
- Every user-owned row has an `owner` FK. Query with `Model.objects.filter(owner=request.user)` or the helpers in `core/validators/ownership.py` (`_owned_queryset`, `_owned_object_or_404`, `_child_owned_*`). No staff or superuser bypass.
- Child rows inherit ownership through their parent (e.g. salary entries via `company__owner`).
- Start every API view with `_api_auth_required(request)`. CSRF is on everywhere except the Paymob webhook. Login attempts use django-axes.
- Settings and secrets: AI provider keys are encrypted (`credential_encryption.py`); never log or return them. `.env` and `db.sqlite3` are never edited.
- Non-admins only get a whitelist from `/api/settings/`. Source-code tools of the AI are sysadmin-only.
- Every security-relevant change needs a test proving user A cannot read or change user B's data (pattern in the tests of `ai/tests/test_ai_chat_manage.py`).


## Skill: balances-and-net-worth
# Balances and net worth
- `BalanceEntry` (`core/models/balance/balance_entry.py`): owner, title, `balance_type` (cash / bank / gold / certificate), bank, currency, amount (Decimal 18,2).
- Money moves through `core/services/expenses/expense_balance_helpers.py` (`_apply_expense_balance_delta`) and the balance services in `core/services/balance/`. Never change a balance with a raw `.update()` outside these helpers.
- Net worth: `core/services/balance/net_worth_calculations.py` and `net_worth_service/`. These are financial calculations: do not change without approval.
- Cash expenses and bank expenses both reduce a matching `BalanceEntry`; a missing matching entry raises `matching_balance_entry_not_found`, too little money raises `insufficient_balance`.
- Always use `Decimal`, never `float`, for stored money. Amounts are kept in their own currency plus `amount_base` in the user's base currency (`get_user_base_code(owner)`).
- Latest exchange rates: `core/services/shared/latest_rates.latest_exchange_rates()`; never `order_by("-fetched_at").first()` inline.
- Tests: `core/tests/balance/`.


## Skill: testing
# Testing
- Django tests: `core/tests/<area>/test_*.py`; run `python manage.py test core.tests.<area>` (targeted first, then the full suite). One known sandbox-only failure: the Playwright single-page-failure-isolation test; known on main: `test_speech_api` Arabic Piper test.
- Users in tests get currencies/categories automatically: use `get_or_create`, not `create`.
- Static checks: `python -m pyflakes core tests scripts wealthflow doc_engine manage.py`, `npm run validate`, `python manage.py check`, `makemigrations --check`.

example.answer: build (lines 88–116) validates a single proposed code change and returns the payload the confirm-card and the later write (apply) need — it writes nothing. Steps: 1) check_path validates the repo-relative path (no absolute paths, no '..', stays inside ROOT, not in blocked/hidden dirs, allowed extension, not protected). 2) Enforces MAX_TEXT (8000 chars) on content/old_str/new_str. 3) If `content` is given and the file doesn't exist → 'add' op: normalizes line endings, checks the file-line limit and syntax (ast for .py, json.loads for .json), returns op/path/content/lines. 4) If the file is missing and no content → error asking to pass `content`. 5) If the file exists, `content` is rejected (must use old_str/new_str); old must be a non-empty string, new a string. 6) Reads the current file, rewrites old/new with the file's existing line endings (_like), and requires old_str to appear exactly once (count==1) to guarantee an unambiguous replacement. 7) Computes `after = current.replace(old, new, 1)`; errors if nothing changes; re-checks the line limit (only if the file grows past max_file_lines) and that the result parses. 8) Returns op='edit' with old_str/new_str (line-ending-normalized), base_sha (sha256 of the current content — the concurrency token apply later compares against), old/new, and a '+X / -Y' lines summary. In short: build is the dry-run/validator that turns a model-proposed change into a checked, confirmable action; apply is what actually writes it.

## Skill: balances-and-net-worth
# Balances and net worth
- `BalanceEntry` (`core/models/balance/balance_entry.py`): owner, title, `balance_type` (cash / bank / gold / certificate), bank, currency, amount (Decimal 18,2).
- Money moves through `core/services/expenses/expense_balance_helpers.py` (`_apply_expense_balance_delta`) and the balance services in `core/services/balance/`. Never change a balance with a raw `.update()` outside these helpers.
- Net worth: `core/services/balance/net_worth_calculations.py` and `net_worth_service/`. These are financial calculations: do not change without approval.
- Cash expenses and bank expenses both reduce a matching `BalanceEntry`; a missing matching entry raises `matching_balance_entry_not_found`, too little money raises `insufficient_balance`.
- Always use `Decimal`, never `float`, for stored money. Amounts are kept in their own currency plus `amount_base` in the user's base currency (`get_user_base_code(owner)`).
- Latest exchange rates: `core/services/shared/latest_rates.latest_exchange_rates()`; never `order_by("-fetched_at").first()` inline.
- Tests: `core/tests/balance/`.


## Skill: django-architecture
# Django architecture (WealthFlow)
- Stack: Django 6 backend, vanilla-JS single-page app (no framework), SQLite in the repo (`db.sqlite3` tracked on purpose, never edit it).
- Layers: `core/models/` (one file or folder per area) -> `core/services/<area>/` (business rules) -> `core/views/` (thin JSON views) -> `core/urls/*_urls.py` (all routes `api/...`).
- Views are class-based `View`s returning `JsonResponse`. Start each handler with `_api_auth_required(request)` (from `core.validators`); body via `parse_json_body(request)`.
- Business logic belongs in a service class, never in a view. Reuse the existing service the screen already uses (e.g. `ExpenseService`) instead of writing to models directly.
- Plan gating: wrap routes with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (`core/services/billing`). Sysadmin-only views use `SysadminRequiredMixin`.
- App settings live in `AppSettings` (`AppSettings.get(key, default, user=...)`); `user=None` = global. The AI app's own `ai_*`/`speech_*`/`image_gen_*` settings live in `ai.models.AISetting` (same get/set API). Prefer a UI setting over `.env`.
- `ai/` must not import `core`: WealthFlow-specific AI code lives in `core/ai_pack` and plugs in through `settings.AI_PACKS`; host answers (admin check, audit, currency) are `AI_*` hooks in `wealthflow/settings.py` (`ai/host.py`).
- Every code file must stay <= 200 lines: split into a package folder with an `__init__.py` that re-exports.
- Shared central services are additive-only: `CurrencyConversionService`, `base_currency.py`, `ExchangeRateHistoryService`, `market_profile.py`, settings access. List every caller before touching one.

example.goal: What does the JavaScript function `showCenterAlert` in `static/js/app/center_alert.js` do? Explain it from the code. Answer only; do not plan or change anything.
example.answer: `showCenterAlert(msg, type = "error")` displays a centered, full-screen overlay alert for blocking validation errors (e.g. certificate balance-deduction failures). Behavior: (1) It finds the mount point `#center-alert-container`; if that element doesn't exist, it falls back to the existing corner toast by calling `showToast(msg, type)` and returns. (2) Otherwise it generates a unique id (`center-alert-<timestamp>`), picks a border color — green (`--accent-green`) when `type === "success"`, red (`--accent-red`) otherwise — and appends an overlay div containing a card with the message, a colored left border, and a close button. (3) It wires up two dismissal paths: clicking the close button, or clicking the overlay background itself (checking `e.target === overlay`) removes the element. There is deliberately no auto-dismiss — the alert stays until the user closes it, because it signals an action the user must take (e.g. fixing a bank/currency mapping or balance). Note: the message `msg` is inserted via template string without HTML escaping, and the function is a standalone addition that does not modify `showToast`/`#toast-container`.

example.goal: What parameters does `handle_certificate_pre_save` in `core/services/certificate/certificate_balance_deduction_service/handlers.py` take, what does it return, and what happens on bad input? Answer only; do not plan or change anything.
example.answer:
handle_certificate_pre_save(sender, instance, **kwargs) — a Django pre_save signal handler.

Parameters:
- sender: the model class that emitted the signal (used to fetch the old row via sender.objects.get(pk=instance.pk)).
- instance: the certificate model instance being saved; the handler reads instance.bank_id, instance.currency_id, instance.owner, instance.amount, instance.status, and instance.pk.
- **kwargs: swallows the remaining signal arguments (e.g. raw, update_fields).

Return value:
- Always returns None (implicitly). Its only side effect besides validation is stashing a snapshot of the old held principal (old_bank_id, old_currency_id, old_held_amount, or None for a new row) on the instance under the attribute _cbs_old_snapshot, which handle_certificate_post_save later consumes and then deletes.

On bad input it does not return an error — it raises (so the save is blocked):
- CertificateBalanceMappingError ("There's no cash balance set up yet for this bank and currency...") if no cash BalanceEntry exists for (instance.bank_id, instance.currency_id, instance.owner) — checked by validate_balance_entry_exists in matching.py.
- CertificateInsufficientBalanceError ("The matching cash balance doesn't have enough funds to cover this certificate's amount...") if the matching cash entry cannot cover the principal to be held (held_amount(instance.amount, instance.status); 0 for a Closed certificate). For updates on the same bank/currency, the previously held amount from the old snapshot is added back first, so only the net delta must be covered — checked by validate_sufficient_balance.

Non-error edge cases: if instance.pk is set but the old row no longer exists (sender.DoesNotExist), the old snapshot is simply None. A closed certificate holds 0, so it never fails the sufficiency check.

{"final": "handle_certificate_pre_save(sender, instance, **kwargs) — a Django pre_save signal handler.

Parameters:
- sender: the model class that emitted the signal (used to fetch the old row via sender.objects.get(pk=instance.pk)).
- instance: the certificate model instance being saved; the handler reads instance.bank_id, instance.currency_id, instance.owner, instance.amount, instance.status, and instance.pk.
- **kwargs: swallows the remaining signal arguments (e.g. raw, update_fields).

Return value:
- Always returns None (implicitly). Its only side effect besides validation is stashing a snapshot of the old held principal (old_bank_id, old_currency_id, old_held_amount, or None for a new row) on the instance under the attribute _cbs_old_snapshot, which handle_certificate_post_save later consumes and then deletes.

On bad input it does not return an error — it raises (so the save is blocked):
- CertificateBalanceMappingError ("There's no cash balance set up yet for this bank and currency...") if no cash BalanceEntry exists for (instance.bank_id, instance.currency_id, instance.owner) — checked by validate_balance_entry_exists in matching.py.
- CertificateInsufficientBalanceError ("The matching cash balance doesn't have enough funds to cover this certificate's amount...") if the matching cash entry cannot cover the principal to be held (held_amount(instance.amount, instance.status); 0 for a Closed certificate). For updates on the same bank/currency, the previously held amount from the old snapshot is added back first, so only the net delta must be covered — checked by validate_sufficient_balance.

Non-error edge cases: if instance.pk is set but the old row no longer exists (sender.DoesNotExist), the old snapshot is simply None. A closed certificate holds 0, so it never fails the sufficiency check."}

## Skill: django-architecture
# Django architecture (WealthFlow)
- Stack: Django 6 backend, vanilla-JS single-page app (no framework), SQLite in the repo (`db.sqlite3` tracked on purpose, never edit it).
- Layers: `core/models/` (one file or folder per area) -> `core/services/<area>/` (business rules) -> `core/views/` (thin JSON views) -> `core/urls/*_urls.py` (all routes `api/...`).
- Views are class-based `View`s returning `JsonResponse`. Start each handler with `_api_auth_required(request)` (from `core.validators`); body via `parse_json_body(request)`.
- Business logic belongs in a service class, never in a view. Reuse the existing service the screen already uses (e.g. `ExpenseService`) instead of writing to models directly.
- Plan gating: wrap routes with `feature_required("allows_ai_workspace")` (`core/services/billing`). Sysadmin-only views use `SysadminRequiredMixin`.
- App settings live in `AppSettings` (`AppSettings.get(key, default, user=...)`); `user=None` = global. The AI app's own `ai_*`/`speech_*`/`image_gen_*` settings live in `ai.models.AISetting` (same get/set API). Prefer a UI setting over `.env`.
- `ai/` must not import `core`: WealthFlow-specific AI code lives in `core/ai_pack` and plugs in through `settings.AI_PACKS`; host answers (admin check, audit, currency) are `AI_*` hooks in `wealthflow/settings.py` (`ai/host.py`).
- Every code file must stay <= 200 lines: split into a package folder with an `__init__.py` that re-exports.
- Shared central services are additive-only: `CurrencyConversionService`, `base_currency.py`, `ExchangeRateHistoryService`, `market_profile.py`, settings access. List every caller before touching one.


## Skill: testing
# Testing
- Django tests: `core/tests/<area>/test_*.py`; run `python manage.py test core.tests.<area>` (targeted first, then the full suite). One known sandbox-only failure: the Playwright single-page-failure-isolation test; known on main: `test_speech_api` Arabic Piper test.
- Users in tests get currencies/categories automatically: use `get_or_create`, not `create`.
- Static checks: `python -m pyflakes core tests scripts wealthflow doc_engine manage.py`, `npm run validate`, `python manage.py check`, `makemigrations --check`.
- Browser E2E: `scripts/run_full_e2e.py --headless` on the owner's PC only. Every change adds a module under `tests/modules/<name>.py`, wired in `scripts/e2e_module_dispatch.py`, `scripts/test_ui_human_full_e2e.py` and `tests/core/reporter.py` (page denominators).
- Never claim a test passed unless its command finished successfully; say plainly what was NOT run.
- Automated gate: `python scripts/agent_verify.py` (checks, targeted tests, pyflakes, migrations, i18n, line limits).

- Write ONLY through `ExpenseService.create_expense / update_expense / delete_expense(…, owner)` in `core/services/expenses/expense_service.py`: they check ownership, convert currency (`CurrencyConversionService.strict_rate`) and adjust the balance in one transaction.
- Errors are `ValueError` codes: `bank_account_required`, `category_not_found`, `matching_balance_entry_not_found`, `insufficient_balance`, `readonly_mirrored_expense`, `exchange_rate_missing`.

- Views: `core/views/expense_views.py`, `expense_category_views.py`, `expense_summary_views.py`. Frontend: `static/js/expenses/`.
- Tests: `core/tests/expenses/`; E2E: `tests/modules/expenses/`.


## Skill: security-and-tenancy
# Security and multi-tenancy

- Child rows inherit ownership through their parent (e.g. salary entries via `company__owner`).
- Start every API view with `_api_auth_required(request)`. CSRF is on everywhere except the Paymob webhook. Login attempts use django-axes.
- Settings and secrets: AI provider keys are encrypted (`credential_encryption.py`); never log or return them. `.env` and `db.sqlite3` are never edited.
- Non-admins only get a whitelist from `/api/settings/`. Source-code tools of the AI are sysadmin-only.
